BURKE COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS 
CALLED MEETING – HEPHZIBAH ANNEXATION 
OCTOBER 16, 2026 
 
The Burke County Board of Commissioners held a Called Meeting on Friday, October 16, 
2026, at 9:00 AM in the Commissioners’ Room of the Burke County Courthouse. Chair 
Evans Martin called the meeting to order at 9:00 AM. Commissioners Kelly, Braswell, and 
Lively were present. County Manager Adam Flakes and County Attorney Adam Nelson were 
also in attendance.  
Invocation was given by Jeffery Thomson. 
Chair Martin explained that representatives of the City of Hephzibah Commission would 
present an overview of the proposed annexation, followed by an opportunity for public 
questions and comments. The City’s representatives introduced themselves as Robert 
Buchwitz, Commission Chair; and Commissioners Jody Boulineau, Ven McFalls, and 
Jordan Rhoades. 
Mr. Buchwitz provided an overview of the City of Hephzibah’s growth and water system 
expansion, noting that discussions with Burke County regarding annexation date back to 
the late 1980s and early 1990s.  He further stated that, in 2012, the city again approached 
Burke County regarding the proposed annexation of areas along Corley Road, Farmers 
Bridge Road, and Story Mill Road to facilitate water system expansion.  Mr. Buchwitz stated 
at that time, Burke County requested the annexation by the 100% method.   
Mr. Buchwitz stated that the City of Hephzibah’s 2018 Comprehensive Plan includes 
provisions for expanding its water system into Burke County. He further stated that, in 2021 
or 2022, Burke County engaged an engineering firm to evaluate the feasibility of the City of 
Hephzibah to supply water to northern Burke County via Keysville Road. Mr. Buchwitz 
explained that the City of Hephzibah would require control over water usage and 
development, necessitating annexation of the proposed service area.   
Mr. Buchwitz explained the contiguity requirements for annexation into the City of 
Hephzibah, stating that nine (9) parcels in Burke County have expressed interest in 
annexation, with an additional seven (7) parcels having submitted petitions for annexation.  
Mr. Buchwitz further stated that property owners who do not wish to be annexed into the 
City of Hephzibah would not be required to do so. 
 
 
Mr. Buchwitz provided additional background on the Keysville water project, dating back to 
the early 1990s. He stated that the City of Keysville received grant funding for the 
installation of a well and water tank but lacked sufficient funds to install the necessary 
water lines. According to Mr. Buchwitz, the City of Hephzibah provided the materials and 
labor needed to complete the water line installation.   
Mr. Buchwitz stated that the proposed project currently appears to be limited to Keysville 
Road, Wright Allen Road, and Farmers Bridge Road, as the proposed water line loop along 
Corley Road would not serve any additional customers at this time.  
Mr. Buchwitz stated that the City of Hephzibah has not levied municipal property taxes 
since the 1970s and funds its operations through Richmond County LOST/SPLOST 
revenues and investment income.  Mr. Buchwitz stated that the City of Hephzibah currently 
employs ten (10) full-time firefighters and seven (7) full-time police officers and indicated 
that the proposed annexation would allow the City to provide enhanced public safety 
services to the affected areas, potentially providing 21-25% cost savings on homeowners 
insurance. 
Chair Martin expressed concerns regarding the proposed annexation, stating that water 
system expansion could be accomplished through an intergovernmental agreement 
between Burke County and the City of Hephzibah without the need for annexation.  
Discussion between the Boards continued regarding the potential loss of LOST and 
TSPLOST revenues resulting from the proposed annexation, with concerns expressed that 
such losses could place an additional financial burden on Burke County and its existing 
municipalities and communities.  Mr. Buchwitz stated that, at this time, he was uncertain 
what oversight measures or safeguards could be established to ensure that such revenues 
would remain in Burke County and not be utilized in Richmond County.  Commissioner 
Braswell questioned the City's long-term plans for the area, noting the significant 
investment required for water line expansion and inquiring whether future development 
was being considered. Mr. Buchwitz responded that no subdivisions or data centers are 
currently planned, no cost analysis has been completed for the proposed water line 
expansion, and there are no opportunities for further annexation into Augusta-Richmond 
County. 
Commissioner Lively inquired whether the City of Hephzibah would be opposed to entering 
into an intergovernmental agreement. Mr. Buchwitz responded that the City's willingness to 
consider such an agreement would depend on its terms, as the City would want to retain 
control of the water system following installation. 
 
 
Manager Flakes expressed concern regarding the potential use of Richmond County tax 
revenues to fund a project in Burke County. He stated that he had no reservations about 
entering into an intergovernmental agreement with the City of Hephzibah; however, his 
primary concerns centered on the proposed annexation and the authority the City would 
have over affected Burke County residents. 
CFO Wiseman requested clarification regarding the City's General Fund and Investment 
Fund balances, expressing concern that the amount of funding derived from Richmond 
County tax revenues was significantly higher than previously believed. 
Chair Martin then opened the floor for public comment. 
Ms. Pamelia Bartlett questioned the potential financial benefits the City of Hephzibah 
would receive from the proposed annexation and expressed concern regarding the 
possibility of future annexation efforts extending further into Burke County. 
Ms. Sara Singletary expressed concern that the proposed annexation could affect all Burke 
County residents through the potential loss of LOST and SPLOST revenues, noting that any 
resulting funding shortfall would need to be addressed through alternative revenue 
sources. She also questioned the return on investment for the proposed water system 
expansion, given the limited number of residents expressing interest in receiving water 
service and inquired whether the City of Keysville could expand its existing water system to 
serve northern Burke County. 
Ms. Carol Johnson expressed her belief that the proposed annexation was primarily about 
control rather than water service expansion and voiced concern that approval could 
establish a precedent for future annexation efforts. 
Mr. Ed Templeton requested a map of the area affected by the proposed annexation, which 
the County displayed for public viewing. He inquired about the number of households that 
could potentially be served by the proposed water line expansion. Mr. Templeton 
questioned whether the fire station on Story Mill Road was staffed 24 hours a day, 365 days 
a year, to which Mr. Buchwitz responded that it was not.  Mr. Templeton further expressed 
concern that there was no guarantee the City of Hephzibah would continue operating 
without levying municipal property taxes, particularly if the City experienced a reduction or 
loss of LOST and SPLOST revenues.  In response, Mr. Buchwitz stated that residents could 
petition for deannexation from the City of Hephzibah. 
Mr. Jeff Phillips inquired about the City of Hephzibah’s long-term growth plans and the 
extent of any potential future expansion. 
 
 
Ms. Rhonda Nickerson questioned why residents in the Wright Allen Road area who would 
be directly affected by the proposed annexation had not received notification. 
Mr. James Neely, Mayor of Keysville, suggested exploring an intergovernmental agreement 
with the City of Hephzibah. 
Mr. Jerry Morgan expressed his belief that government decisions are often driven by 
financial interests and control. 
Mr. Bill Tinley expressed his belief that the City of Hephzibah’s objectives could be 
accomplished through an intergovernmental agreement, potentially providing a mutually 
beneficial solution for both Burke County and the City of Hephzibah. 
Mr. Michael Rogers requested that County Attorney Nelson explain the 60/60 annexation 
rule and its potential implications for property owners who do not wish to be annexed. He 
further requested that the Board of Commissioners deny the City of Hephzibah’s 
annexation request. 
Mr. Seth Schwartz inquired whether the City of Hephzibah operates a water treatment plant 
and questioned whether Burke County could explore an agreement with Richmond County 
to extend water service into the affected area. 
Chair Martin stated that the Board of Commissioners would further discuss and consider 
the proposed annexation, with the matter to be placed on November 10, 2026, regular 
meeting agenda. 
There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 10:26 AM.

I. Background and General Information 
 
The site consists of a 50-acre parcel currently owned by Billy Williams. The 
parcel is identified as Columbia County Parcel # 043 130. Impact Community Church 
wishes to purchase and subdivide the lot to facilitate development of a new church 
location. The church proposes subdividing the existing parcel into 5 parcels of 12.17, 
8.78, 3.00, 4.22, and 21.78 acres (see site map below). The development plan for the 
church includes building a main church building with associated parking and utilities. 
All development is proposed to occur on the 12.17 acre “Lot A” with a frontage on 
Gordon Hwy. The church wishes to rezone Lot A from R-A to S-1 to accommodate 
this development. The remaining parcels will remain R-A and will share a common 
drive with the church. The R-A zoned lots will be developed for residential use at a 
future date.

II. Zoning and Land Use 
 
 The site is currently zoned R-A. The property is bounded to the north by Gordon 
Hwy. On all other sides the parcel is bounded by zone R-A, except for one S-1 parcel. 
The church wishes to rezone “Lot A” as described in the previous section to S-1. A 
zoning map of the site and surrounding area is provided below. 
 
 
 
 
Zoning Map 
 
The S-1 special zoning district is intended “to provide for the proper placement of 
private, semiprivate and public uses which require special consideration because of their 
character, physical setting, size and/or relation to surrounding land uses. Based on the 
proposed land use as a church, the proposed S-1 rezoning is consistent with the S-1 
zoning district. 
 
 
III. Vegetation, Soils and Topography 
 
The parcel presently contains no structures. Lot A is largely free of trees except 
for some trees along the perimeter . The owner proposes to minimize site work and 
intends to retain as much of the existing trees and other natural vegetation as possible.

Soils on the church site are primarily Norfolk loamy sand and Tifton sandy loam . 
A soil scientist has evaluated the soil on each lot for suitability for septic service. Each lot 
was determined to have suitable soils for a septic system . A detailed septic system design 
will be required for each lot. 
 
National Wetland Inventory m aps indicate that a stream  may exist on proposed 
Lot D and Lot E. Based on an aquatic resources determination by our office, there are no 
State waters present on the existing parcel . This matter was coordinated with the 
Columbia County Engineering Services Department and a State waters determination 
letter was issued confirming our findings. 
 
Some possible wetlands exist along the eastern property line of the propo sed Lot 
E. A formal wetland delineation will be required when Lot E is developed.  There are no 
wetlands on proposed Lot A, where the development is proposed. No work is proposed to 
take place in the vicinity of the potential wetlands at this time. 
 
 
IV. Utilities: 
 
Water service to the property will be provided by a new well system . Sanitary 
sewer services will be provided by a septic system. Electrical power, telephone, and cable 
are available along Gordon Highway. 
 
 
V. Floodplain Management 
 
A review of the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) for Columbia County 
indicates that there are no floodplains on or near the development site on proposed Lot A. 
An unstudied Zone A Special Flood Hazard Area does exist on proposed Lots D and E  as 
depicted on FIRM map number 13073C0220E.  A floodplain elevation report will be 
required prior to the development of Lots D and E.

VI. Development Proposal 
 
The development proposal for this site consists of constructing a  church building. 
Parking, a dumpster enclosure, and utilities are proposed in association with the  building. 
The church may potentially  expand its development in the future to include an  
educational/gym building and recreational facilities such as a green space, open field, 
playgrounds, a baseball field, storage, and bathrooms. There is currently no scheduled 
date for these improvements. 
 
The proposed rezoning from R -A to S -1 will change some of the setback 
requirements. The front setback will remain the same. The side and rear setbacks and 
buffers will change. The rear setback will change from 25 f eet to a proposed 30 f eet 
based on S -1 buffers  as described in Columbia County’s Zoning Ordinance . The side 
setbacks will change from 10 f eet to a proposed 30 f eet based on S -1 buffers. Proposed 
setbacks are listed below.

Side:   30 ft.

Buffers: 
 
No buffer requirements currently exist between the R -A zoned parcel and 
adjacent parcels which are all zoned R -A except for one S-1 parcel. As a consequence of  
the rezoning, the buffer requirements for proposed Lot A will change from no buffer 
requirements to 30 ft on all sides.  
 
 
Lot, Architecture and Landscaping Description:   
 
The proposed Lot A  is 12.17 acres in size with a 714 ft frontage along Gordon 
Highway. There are no existing facilities on the property. There is an existing paved 
public road connection. The existing driveway will be improved as required to support 
the church and the four additional lots. Modifications to the existing driveway will be 
submitted to Georgia DOT for review and permitting. 
 
The proposed parking area will be paved and shall include approximately 148 
new parking spaces. Final details regarding the exterior  finish shall be provided to the 
Planning Department for review when the architectural plans are developed. 
 
In order to meet the intent of the County landscape ordinance, additional 
landscaping shall be added along a 20 foot wide section of the frontage and shall be 
clustered, where necessary, to meet the landscape requirements for the site when the 
parking improvements are completed. Specific details regarding the site landscaping shall 
be coordinated during the site plan review phase. 
 
 
Operational Information: 
 
Church services will be held on Sunday mornings between 6 a.m. and 1 p.m. and 
Monday mornings between 9 a.m. and 1 p.m . The church is also open in the evenings for 
groups, but the schedule will change each semester. Th e primary assembly area of the 
church will be approximately 4,661 square feet and will have a seating capacity of 300. 
The overall building is approximately 16,000 square feet in size.

1.Sampling Requirements. This permit requires the monitoring of nephelometric turbidity in receiving water(s) or outfalls in accordance with this permit. This
section is applicable to Primary Permittees with a total planned disturbance equal to or greater than one (1) acre and Tertiary Permittees with a total planned
disturbance equal to or greater than five (5) acres. This section is not applicable to Secondary Permittees. The following procedures constitute EPD's guidelines
for sampling turbidity.
a.Sampling Requirements shall include the following:
(1).A USGS topographic map, a topographic map or a drawing (referred to as a topographic map) that is a scale equal to or more detailed than a
1:24000 map showing the location of the site or the common development; (a) the location of all perennial and intermittent streams and other water
bodies as shown on a USGS topographic map, and all other perennial and intermittent streams and other water bodies located during mandatory field
verification, into which the stormwater is discharged and (b) the receiving water and/or outfall sampling locations. When the permittee has chosen to
use a USGS topographic map and the receiving water(s) is not shown on the USGS topographic map, the location of the receiving water(s) must be
hand-drawn on the USGS topographic map from where the stormwater(s) enters the receiving water(s) to the point where the receiving water(s)
combines with the first blue line stream shown on the USGS topographic map;
(2).The analytical method used to collect and analyze the samples including quality control/quality assurance procedures. This narrative must
include precise sampling methodology for each sampling location;
(3).When the permittee has determined that some or all outfalls will be sampled, a rationale must be included on the Plan for the NTU limit(s)
selected from Appendix
A.This rationale must include the size of the construction site, the calculation of the size of the surface water drainage area, and the type of
receiving water(s) (i.e., trout stream or supporting warm water fisheries); and
(4).Any additional information EPD determines necessary to be part of the Plan. EPD will provide written notice to the permittee of the information
necessary and the timeline for submittal.
b.Sample Type. All sampling shall be collected by “grab samples" and the analysis of these samples must be conducted in accordance with methodology and
test procedures established by 40 CFR Part 136 (unless other test procedures have been approved); the guidance document titled "NPDES Storm Water
Sampling Guidance Document, EPA 833- B-92-001" and guidance documents that may be prepared by the EPD.
(1).Sample containers should be labeled prior to collecting the samples.
(2).Samples should be well mixed before transferring to a secondary container.
(3).Large mouth, clean and rinsed glass or plastic jars should be used for collecting samples. The jars should be cleaned thoroughly to avoid
contamination.
(4).Manual, automatic or rising stage sampling may be utilized. Samples required by this permit should be analyzed immediately, but in no case
later than 48 hours after collection. However, samples from automatic samplers must be collected no later than the next business day after their
accumulation, unless flow through automated analysis is utilized. If automatic sampling is utilized and the automatic sampler is not activated during the
qualifying event, the permittee must utilize manual sampling or rising stage sampling during the next qualifying event. Dilution of samples is not
required. Samples may be analyzed using a direct reading, properly calibrated turbidimeter. Samples are not required to be cooled.
(5).Sampling and analysis of the receiving water(s) or outfalls beyond the minimum frequency stated in this permit must be reported to EPD as
specified in Part IV.E.
c.Sampling Points.
(1).For construction activities the Primary Permittee with a total planned disturbance equal to or greater than one (1) acre and Tertiary Permittee
with a total planned disturbance equal to or greater than five (5) acres must sample all receiving water(s), or all outfall(s), or a combination of receiving
water(s) and outfall(s). Sampling points shall be located on applicable pages of the Initial, Intermediate, and Final phase of the Erosion, Sedimentation
and Pollution Control Plans.
Samples taken for the purpose of compliance with this permit shall be representative of the monitored activity and representative of the water quality of
the receiving water(s) and/or the stormwater outfalls using the following minimum guidelines:
(a).The upstream sample for each receiving water(s) must be taken immediately upstream of the confluence of the first stormwater discharge
from the permitted activity (i.e., the discharge farthest upstream at the site) but downstream of any other stormwater discharges not associated with
the permitted activity. Where appropriate, several upstream samples from across the receiving water(s) may need to be taken and the arithmetic
average of the turbidity of these samples used for the upstream turbidity value.
(b).The downstream sample for each receiving water(s) must be taken downstream of the confluence of the last stormwater discharge from
the permitted activity (i.e., the discharge farthest downstream at the site) but upstream of any other stormwater discharge not associated with the
permitted activity. Where appropriate, several downstream samples from across the receiving water(s) may need to be taken and the arithmetic
average of the turbidity of these samples used for the downstream turbidity value.
(c).Ideally the samples should be taken from the horizontal and vertical center of the receiving water(s) or the stormwater outfall channel(s).
(d).Care should be taken to avoid stirring the bottom sediments in the receiving water(s) or in the outfall stormwater channel.
(e).The sampling container should be held so that the opening faces upstream.
(f).The samples should be kept free from floating debris.
(g).Permittees do not have to sample sheet flow that flows onto undisturbed natural areas or areas stabilized by the project. For purposes of
this section, stabilized shall mean, for unpaved areas and areas not covered by permanent structures and areas located outside the waste disposal
limits of a landfill cell that has been certified by EPD for waste disposal, 100% of the soil surface is uniformly covered in permanent vegetation
with a density of 70% or greater, or landscaped according to the Plan (uniformly covered with landscaping materials in planned landscaped areas),
or equivalent permanent stabilization measures as defined in the Manual (excluding a crop of annual vegetation and seeding of target crop
perennials appropriate for the region).
(h).All sampling pursuant to this permit must be done in such a way (including generally accepted sampling methods, locations, timing, and
frequency) as to accurately reflect whether stormwater runoff from the construction site is in compliance with the standard set forth in Parts or
III.D.4.or III.D.5., whichever is applicable.
d.Sampling Frequency.
(1).The Primary Permittee with a total planned disturbance equal to or greater than one (1) acre and Tertiary Permittee with a total planned
disturbance equal to or greater than five (5) acres must sample in accordance with the Plan at least once for each rainfall event described below. For a
qualifying event, the permittee shall sample at the beginning of any stormwater discharge to a monitored receiving water and/or from a monitored
outfall within forty-five (45) minutes or as soon as possible.
(2).However, where manual and automatic sampling are impossible (as defined in this permit), or are beyond the permittee's control, the permittee
shall take samples as soon as possible, but in no case more than twelve (12) hours after the beginning of the stormwater discharge.
(3).Sampling by the permittee shall occur for the following qualifying events:
(a).For each area of the site that discharges to a receiving water or from an outfall, the first rain event that reaches or exceeds 0.5 inch with a
stormwater discharge that allows for sampling during normal business hours after all clearing and grubbing operations have been completed, but
prior to completion of mass grading operations, in the drainage area of the location selected as the sampling location;
(b).In addition to (a) above, for each area of the site that discharges to a receiving water or from an outfall, the first rain event that reaches or
exceeds 0.5 inch with a stormwater discharge that occurs during normal business hours either 90 days after the first sampling event or after all
mass grading operations have been completed, but prior to submittal of a NOT, in the drainage area of the location selected as the sampling
location, whichever comes first;
(c).At the time of sampling performed pursuant to (a) and (b) above, if BMPs in any area of the site that discharges to a receiving water or
from an outfall are not properly designed, installed and maintained, corrective action shall be defined and implemented within two (2) business
days, and turbidity samples shall be taken from discharges from that area of the site
for each subsequent rain event that reaches or exceeds 0.5 inch during normal business hours* until the selected turbidity standard is attained, or
until post-rain event inspections determine that BMPs are properly designed, installed and maintained;
(d).Where sampling pursuant to (a), (b) or (c) above is required but not possible (or not required because there was no discharge), the Primary
Permittee, in accordance with Part IV.D.4.a.(6)., or the Tertiary Permittee, in accordance with Part IV.D.4.c.(6)., must include a written
justification in the inspection report of why sampling was not performed. Providing this justification does not relieve the permittee of any
subsequent sampling obligations under (a), (b) or (c) above; and
(e).Existing construction activities, i.e., those that are occurring on or before the effective date of this permit, that have met the sampling
required by (a) above shall sample in accordance with (b). Those existing construction activities that have met the sampling required by (b) above
shall not be required to conduct additional sampling other than as required by (c) above.
*Note that the Permittee may choose to meet the requirements of (a) and (b) above by collecting turbidity samples from any rain event that reaches
or exceeds 0.5 inch and allows for sampling at any time of the day or week.

1.Inspections.
a.Primary Permittee.
(1).Each day when any type of construction activity has taken place at a Primary Permittee's site, certified personnel provided by the Primary
Permittee shall inspect: (a) all areas at the Primary Permittee's site where petroleum products are stored, used, or handled for spills and leaks from
vehicles and equipment and (b) all locations at the Primary Permittee's site where vehicles enter or exit the site for evidence of off-site sediment
tracking. These inspections must be conducted until a Notice of Termination is submitted.
(2).Measure and record rainfall within disturbed areas of the site that have not met final stabilization once every 24 hours except any non-working
Saturday, non- working Sunday and non-working Federal holiday. The data collected for the purpose of compliance with this permit shall be
representative of the monitored activity and provided to the Secondary Permittee, if applicable. Measurement of rainfall may be suspended if all areas
of the site have undergone final stabilization or established a crop of annual vegetation and a seeding of target perennials appropriate for the region.
(3).Certified personnel (provided by the Primary Permittee) shall inspect the following at least once every seven (7) calendar days: (a) disturbed
areas of the Primary Permittee's construction site; (b) areas used by the Primary Permittee for storage of materials that are exposed to precipitation; and
(c) structural control measures. Erosion and sediment control measures identified in the Plan applicable to the Primary Permittee's site shall be observed
to ensure that they are operating correctly. Certified personnel shall also conduct inspections within 24 hours of the end of a storm that is 0.5 inches
rainfall or greater (unless such storm ends after 5:00 PM on any Friday or on any non-working Saturday, non-working Sunday or any non-working

Summary and Recommendation 
Owners and applicants Jonathan and Amy Slagle request a Provisional Home Occupation for Tax Map 
051 Parcel 050, 5 +/- acres located at 726 Baker Place Road and currently zoned R -A (Residential 
Agricultural), to operate a gunsmithing business including a machine shop from the subject parcel.  
 
The property is located on the east side of Baker Place Road and is currently zoned R-A (Residential 
Agricultural). Property to the north is zoned PRD (Planned Residential Development) for future phases 
of the Tillery Park subdivision; property to the south is zoned R -A, as is property directly across Baker 
Place Road to the west. Nearby property to the northwest is zoned S-1 (Special) for a future quarry.  
 
The applicant proposes to operate L3 Rifles, LLC, from the subject property. This is a relocation of an 
existing business currently operating in Richmond County to the applicant’s home location. This 
business machines non- firearm parts as well as perform ing gunsmithing services such as threading 
and replacing rifle barrels. Gunsmiths are permitted as customary home occupations when their work 
takes place inside the residence, however, in this case t he business would be operated in a portion of 
a proposed 1200 square foot metal building near the southwest corner of the property. Use of this 
separate building requires review and approval by the Planning Commission before the business 
license can be issued.  
 
The proposed metal building is 30 x 40, totaling 1200 square feet, which is just under 50% of the area 
of the house and meets the provisional home occupation requirements.  This type of building is 
permitted on this parcel provided it meets the building setbacks, which are a minimum of 90 feet from 
the centerline of the road and 10 feet from the side property lines. The applicant has also indicated that 
the business operations will operate from only a portion of this building, with the remainder used for 
storage related to the primary residential use. The applicant has indicated that there are only two 
manually operated pieces of equipment related to the business, and that no noise should be heard from 
adjacent properties.  
 
The applicant has indicated an existing informal access point on the concept plan but has confirmed 
that any customers coming to the site would use the existing driveway. However, the applicant has

burdensome use of existing streets, transportation facilities, utilities or schools. 
It is not anticipated that the proposed use will cause a burden on existing streets, utilities, 
schools, or transportation facilities.  
 
5. If the local government has an adopted land use plan, whether the zoning proposal is in 
conformity with the policy and intent of the land use plan.

neighborhoods, such as Tillery Park to the north of the subject property . The requested 
Provisional Home Occupation is a use allowed by right for customary home occupations; the 
only change is the use of an accessory structure. Larger acreage properties typically have such 
structures where hobbies or other work are performed; the requested Provisional Home 
Occupation does not change the character of the property from the residential intent of this 
Character Area.  
 
6. Whether there are other existing or changing conditions affecting the use and 
development of the property which give supporting grounds for either approval or 
disapproval of the zoning proposal. 
Staff is not aware of any at this time. 
 
7. Whether the proposal reflects a reasonable balance between the promotion of health, 
safety, and welfare against the right to unrestricted use of property. 
The proposal meets this test.

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner Andrea W. Timmerman and applicant Eric W. Clark request a variance to Sections 90 -98 List 
of lot & structure requirements and 90-139 Buffers & screening for property located at 436 Furys Ferry 
Road, Tax Map 082A Parcel 059B, 0.3 +/- acres, and currently split zoned P-1 (Professional) and C-2 
(General Commercial). The applicant is requesting the variance to reduce the building setbacks and to 
reduce the buffer against residential property to allow proposed additions to the existing building.  A 
companion rezoning has also been applied for under RZ26- 10-04 as having a parcel zoned with one 
zoning classification is simpler for both Columbia County and the property owner to address the 
development of that parcel. The applicant has included a concept plan showing the proposed building 
additions to the current dental office and an addendum explaining the variances.  
 
The subject property is located on the west side of Furys Ferry Road. The parcels to the west, 1106 
Furys Lane and the retention pond are also split zoned P -1 and C -2 as per files RZ86 -03-03A and 
RZ86-03-03 respectively. When this rezoning action was taken in 1986, the P -1 zoning was meant to 
act as a separation between the residential area to the north and the C -2 zoning. Other properties to 
the south are zoned C-2. Surrounding properties to the north are zoned R-3 (Single Family Residential) 
and are part of the Wexford Subdivision. Properties across Furys Ferry Road are zoned C-2.  
 
Per the provided concept plan, the applicant proposes to build two additions to the current dental office. 
One addition is planned along the elevation facing the residence to the north and wraps around the 
corner to the west.  The second addition is planned along the elevation facing Furys Lane. With the 
building expansions being restricted to the grassed areas on site, the existing parking spaces will not 
be impacted and no changes are proposed. With the increase in floor area of approximately 620 square 
feet, for an additional doctor’s office and two treatment rooms, totaling two doctors’ offices and six 
treatment rooms, the office will still meet the minimum parking standards required by code.

the existing covered porch area with steps to the west encroaches approximately 5 feet into the 10-foot 
side required setback. The variance request, if approved, would remedy this non-compliance.  
 
The proposed addition to the north will require a buffer reduction to 10 feet from the north property line 
to allow the building expansion. The side setback requirement in the code is 10 feet but as the buffer

the front property line. The front setback from Furys Ferry Road is required to be 125 feet and this is in

The plat shows a 10 -foot drainage and utility easement along the north property line and a 5- foot

Staff does have some concerns with the request  related to site design.  The existing use is being

would be required for County review prior to the issuance of site and building permits for the building 
expansion. If the variance request is approved, the next step will be the engineered plan submittal to 
the Plan Review Department and that will address any technical concerns. The Fire Marshal has 
included a comment that there does not appear to be an existing fire hydrant within the distance 
required by code. The building expansion is currently at a preliminary design stage and the site design

ITEM: Rename the existing Beehive Drive to Willingham Drive and the existing Willingham Drive to 
Willingham Circle, subject to variances to Columbia County Code Sections 18-236 Purpose and 
Administration, and 18-238 Renaming and Procedures 
  
BACKGROUND: Members of the Willingham Family made a presentation and a request to the Columbia 
County Commission at the commission meeting on July 7, 2026.  Their request was for the existing 
Beehive Drive and Willingham Drive to be renamed in honor of their ancestor and family patriarch, based 
on the family’s long-standing residency on the road and contributions to the community. The commission 
subsequently determined that this action is the best interests of the community, and their recommendation 
is that Beehive Drive, a public road located off Mistletoe Road, shall be renamed to Willingham 
Drive.  Likewise, the current Willingham Drive, a private drive easement located off Beehive Drive, shall be 
renamed to Willingham Circle. 
 
Due to the historical and familial nature of the property ownership for the majority of the owners on this road 
(as described in Section 18-238(b)), variances are requested to the following code sections: 
 
•    Section 18-236 - Purpose and administration, in which no two roads shall have the same or similar 
name. 
•    Section 18-238 - Renaming and procedures, in which renaming shall require the concurrence of 100% 
ownership of adjacent properties.

Sec. 18-236. Purpose and administration. 
(a) The purpose of this article is to provide a uniform policy for naming and renaming roads, structures, and 
facilities within Columbia County, Georgia as well as ensuring ease of identification for law enforcement, fire, 
rescue, and emergency medical service personnel in Columbia County, Georgia. Secondarily, this article 
serves to establish standardization of identification to enhance county records of utility service, construction, 
permitting, licensing, and valuation. Finally, this article shall also provide a uniform policy for the 
establishment of memorials, monuments, sculptures, works of art, and park benches on county owned 
designated property.  
(b) This article will be administered by the individual/individuals, who will be designated by the deputy county 
administrator, referred to herein as "agency." The agency will administer the naming and renaming of roads, 
structures, and facilities and the establishment of memorials, sculptures, works of art, and park benches on 
county owned designated property in accordance with the policies set forth herewith. The agency will also 
be responsible for maintaining an official record of this article.  
(c) (1) All roads that serve three or more structures or lots will be named regardless of whether the ownership is 
public or private.  
(2) As used herein, a "road" refers to any highway, bridge, road, street, avenue, lane, private way, or 
similar paved, gravel, or dirt thoroughfare, and "property" refers to any property on which a structure 
has been erected or placed or may be lawfully erected or placed.  
(3) A road name assigned by Columbia County will not constitute or imply acceptance of the road as a 
public way.  
(4) Agency may solicit the involvement of those residents of affected neighborhoods in determining new 
or modified street names.  
(5) No two roads will be given the same name or similar sounding name.  
(6) Each road will have the same name throughout its entire length, when feasible, as determined by the 
agency.

Sec. 18-237. Naming and procedures. 
(a) Naming.  
(1) New roads.  
a. New road names submitted by a developer will be reviewed and approved during the plan review 
process. New road names being initiated by Columbia County will be considered at a scheduled 
committee meeting with final approval being considered by the board of commissioners.  
b. New road names submitted by individual property owners or groups for naming a private 
easement, private road, private street, private avenue, private lane, private way, or similar 
private paved, gravel, or dirt thoroughfare will be considered by making application to the 
agency. Once the application is received, it will be scheduled for the next available committee 
meeting with final approval considered by the board of commissioners.  
(2) Honorary road names.  
a. Honorary road names submitted by an individual or group will be considered by making 
application to the agency. Once the application is received, it will be scheduled for the next 
available committee meeting with final approval considered by the board of commissioners.  
(3) County owned buildings and facilities.  
a. The naming of county owned buildings and facilities will be designated by the Columbia County 
Board of Commissioners by resolution adopted by majority vote.  
b. County buildings or facilities being named or given a title will include but not be limited to 
buildings, areas in buildings, and recreational facilities.  
c. Official names belonging to Columbia County, Georgia will remain the same unless changed by 
the board of commissioners upon relocation or change in function of the building or facility.  
d. The naming of county owned buildings and facilities after individuals is discouraged with the 
following exception:  
1. Deceased person(s) who brought honor to Columbia County, Georgia or made a significant 
monetary or other significant contribution to the development of the county, a county 
building, or a county facility will be considered. Such monetary gift shall at a minimum have 
represented 25 percent of the total county commitment of costs as established by the 
engineering services division.  
e. The naming of a building or facility will be effective for the useful life of the building or facility so 
long as it is used for the purpose for which it was used at the time of the gift. At the end of the 
useful life of the building or facility and/or the cessation of the use in effect at the time of the 
gift, Columbia County, Georgia may rename the building or facility.  
(b) Procedures.  
(1) Roads.  
a. The developer shall submit to the agency during the plan review process, the proposed road 
names to be utilized within the subdivision or commercial development.  
b. Agency will notify the developer of the proposed names that are acceptable once the agency has 
reviewed the proposed names and cross checked them against the current county road index.

ITEM: Purchase of Genetec Servers from Dell for Life Cycle Replacement 
  
BACKGROUND: Columbia County maintains multiple servers and archivers that support the County’s 
Genetec camera solutions for traffic and security cameras. This equipment is replaced as part of the 
County’s equipment lifecycle program to prevent obsolescence and equipment failure / security risks that 
arise from using older hardware. 
 
This agenda item is intended to replace four pieces of equipment, two of which are storage archivers and 
two of which are directory servers that are the core of the system.  These systems are nearing the end of 
their useful life and need to be replaced. 
 
This purchase is made from Dell Technologies and is authorized under Georgia End User Computing 
Agreement (Georgia State Contract) Contract Code C000000493100, Customer Agreement # 99999-
SPD0000161-0004. 
 
The cost of this equipment is $67,473.55, funded through 2023-2028 SPLOST funds allocated for Camera 
Lifecycle and System Expansion. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval. 
  
COMMITTEE COMMENTS: Forward to Consent Agenda. 
  
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION / MOTION: Approved the purchase from Dell for life cycle replacement 
of Genetec Servers in the amount of $67,473.55; 28520.38.090.

Road Suite 10 
  
BACKGROUND: In 2023, Yurui Huang was granted a business license for oriental massage. 
On February 25, 2025, Code Enforcement issued a Stop Work Order on the business due to an expired 
massage operator license.  
On August 5, 2026, Code Enforcement issued Ms. Huang a citation for failing to supervise.  
On August 20, 2026, a letter was sent to Ms. Huang stating it was Columbia County's intention to revoke 
her massage operator and business licenses for violations of county ordinance Section 22-75. 
On September 3, 2026, the Planning Commission held a public hearing and revoked the massage operator 
and business licenses. 
On September 23, 2026, Yurui Huang requested her existing business license at 4158 Washington Road to 
be reinstated limited to beauty and esthetic services. 
 
Per county ordinance Section 22-158 (d), the denial, suspension or revocation under this article shall entitle 
the person applying for or holding the business license to a hearing before the Columbia County Board of 
Commissioners within 45 days after receipt by the county of written notice of appeal.  A notice of appeal 
pursuant to this subsection must be delivered to the clerk of the Columbia County Commission within 30 
days of the denial, suspension or revocation.  Any person aggrieved by a decision or order by the county, 
after exhausting his administrative remedies, shall have the right to appeal de novo to the Superior Court of 
Columbia County.

Summary and Recommendation 
Suite 10 at 4158 Washington Road currently is occupied by the massage business known as Oriental 
Massage. At present, this business is operated by Yurui Huang under Xingda Wellness, LLC. Ms. 
Huang received a Conditional Use for Massage (RZ23- 07-01) in August, 2023 after taking ownership 
of the business from the previous owner who had permitted multiple unlicensed massage therapists to 
operate at the business. Ms. Huang received her business license shortly after in 2023.  
On February 25, 2025, Licensing notified Code Enforcement of an anonymous complaint stating 
Oriental Massage was hiring employees who are not licensed massage therapists. Code Enforcement 
Officer Dennis West visited the location and found 3 employees on site and the owner not present. Mr. 
West was unable to identify one of the females , however, he confirmed the other two did not possess 
MOL’s. Ms. Huang met Mr. West on site and stated she was aware that the license had expired and 
she should not be operating. Code Enforcement posted a Stop Work Order on the business and 
remained on site until all employees had vacated and business doors were locked. Ms. Huang 
renewed her MOL and the business license was iss ued on March 13, 2025. No further action was 
taken at this time, however Ms. Huang was given verbal warning that future violations would result in 
citations. 
On August 5, 2026, Code Enforcement received another c omplaint of employees operating without 
holding proper licensing at Oriental Massage. Code Enforc ement conducted a compliance check 
on August 6th and found one male employee, Yehui Ni, actively providing a massage and three 
other females on site. The business owner, Ms. Huang, again was not at the location. Ms. Huang 
arrived on site after being contacted by one of the females. Code Enforcement officers 
requested Columbia County Sheriff’s Office to assist in obtaining identification for all individuals on 
site. After identifying all individuals, a citation was issued to Mr. Ni for providing a massage without 
proper licensing and to Ms. Huang for failing to supervise. Arraignment date is set for August 19, 
2026. 
Per Section 22-158 Revocation or suspension of business license, any license granted shall be 
subject to revocation or suspens ion for caus e. When there is, in the opinion of the Dev elopment 
Services Director, cause to revoke or suspend a business license, a written notice of intention to 
revoke or suspend shall be furnished not less than ten days before the meeting of the Planning 
Commission. A 
September 3rd, 2026 
letter was hand delivered to the business address on Friday, August 21st  and sent via Certified Mail to 
the business address also on Friday, August 21st. This notification was well within the ten days’ notice 
required before the revocation hearing required per Code.  
P
er Section 22-158 Revocation or suspension of business license, cause for revocation or suspension 
shall include, but not be limited to, the following actions by the business license holder:  
1. P
roviding false or forged information to the licensing official in obtaining a business license
under this article.
2. Impersonating a business license holder.
3. Using or attempting to use a business license that has expired or been revoked.
4. Violation of any provision of this article.
C
olumbia County is recommending revocation of the business license for Xingda Wellness, LLC dba 
Oriental Massage due to the violations that occurred under the current Massage Operator’s License.  
D
ue to these findings, staff recommends revocation of the Business License for Xingda Wellness, LLC 
dba Oriental Massage.

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner and applicant Wendell Mark Boyd requests a rezoning from R-2 (Single Family Residential) to 
C-1 (Neighborhood Commercial ) for property located at 4391 Hereford Farm  Road, Tax map 072A 
Parcel 058, 0.79 +/- acres. The applicant has indicated there are no development plans for the property 
at this time. If rezoned, the property would be included within the Evans Town Center Overlay District 
(ETCOD).   
 
The subject property is located on the north side of Hereford Farm Road near its intersection with North 
Belair Road and is currently zoned R -2 (Single Family Residential). The previously existing house on 
the property has been demolished in preparation for the widening of Hereford Farm Road, and the 
property is vacant of permanent structures. Adjacent properties are zoned C -1 to the east where the 
applicant owns an existing C-1 multitenant parcel, C-2 (General Commercial) to the north, and R -2 to 
the west.  
 
The applicant has provided a short narrative explaining that the current intent with the rezoning is to 
combine the subject parcel with his adjacent property and install landscaping or other permeable 
surface on the property. There are currently no building plans for the property, although development 
of the site may be revisited after the widening of Hereford Farm Road is complete. 
 
Per the recorded plat, the parcel is 91 feet wide; the minimum frontage and minimum width at the front 
setback line in the C -1 district is 100 feet. The property therefore does not meet the minimum 
requirements to be developed as a standalone commercial pr operty, particularly with residential 
property adjacent which would necessitate larger setbacks and buffers than adjacent similarly zoned 
property, further reducing the buildable area on the lot. Effectively, this means the only viable path for 
potentially rezoning this property is combining it with the adjacent property as the applicant has 
proposed. If the rezoning is approved, this combination will need to take place promptly, and a condition 
is proposed to that effect.

The site currently contains a gravel driveway being used as secondary access for the adjacent C -1 
property. The applicant intends to retain the use of the driveway for the overall combined parcel and 
has indicated that he may install additional parking on this lot in the future. The Hereford Farm Road 
widening project does include a driveway cut for the subject parcel;  however, it is planned based on 
the property’s current residential zoning. Both the width and placement of the driveway would likely 
need to be modified for commercial acces s; a condition is proposed to clarify that the applicant would 
be responsible for the site plan and improvements required for the proposed commercial driveway. Any 
parking to be installed would also need to be shown on a civil site plan and would need to be paved to 
County standards, with appropriate landscape strips, parking lot landscaping, and stormwater 
management. To be clear, the existing gravel driveway does not meet code and is not approved; if the 
rezoning is disapproved, the required buffer between these two parcels will need to be installed for the 
entirety of the property line, which will remove this access point for the existing commercial property.  
 
The site also currently contains several shipping containers being used for storage. The applicant has 
indicated that these contain final construction material and are in the process of being liquidated; of 
note, this type of storage is not permitted under  either the current residential zoning or the requested 
C-1 zoning, so regardless of the outcome of the rezoning request, these storage containers must be 
removed from the property. The applicant has additionally indicated they would like the ability to have 
temporary storage on this property; the C -1 zoning district does not permit outdoor storage, so this 
intended use cannot be approved with the current rezoning request, and a proposed condition clarifies 
that this type of use is not permitted on this property.  
 
The property is located within the Town Center Character Area on the Future Development plan; this 
character area includes commercial activity, mixed use development, and entertainment venues such 
as the Performing Arts Center and the Lady A pavilion. This character area serves as the primary hub 
of Evans and is intended to have a concentration of destinations and a pedestrian-oriented mix of uses 
including retail, offices, commercial, and residential. In that respect, the proposed commercial zoning 
is appropriate in this character area.  
 
Due to the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends to approve with conditions the request for a 
rezoning from R-2 (Single Family Residential) to C-1 (Neighborhood Commercial) for property located 
at 4391 Hereford Farm Road, Tax map 072A Parcel 058, 0.79 +/- acres.

Criteria for Evaluation of Rezoning Proposal 
 
1. Whether the zoning proposal will permit a use that is suitable in view of the zoning and 
development of adjacent and nearby property.  
The subject property is located on the north side of Hereford Farm Road and is bordered by 
commercially zoned properties on two sides, with adjacent residential properties to the west. 
The C-1 zoning district is typically considered compatible with nearby residential uses, so the 
requested zoning should be suitable in view of the nearby properties’ zoning.  
 
2. Whether the zoning proposal will adversely affect the existing use or usability of 
adjacent or nearby property.  
The zoning proposal should not adversely impact the usability of adjacent or nearby properties. 
The proposed condition will ensure that the C -1 property has sufficient space for the required 
buffers and setbacks to provide the required separation from the adjacent residences. 
 
3. Whether the zoning proposal is compatible with the purpose and intent of the 
Foundations for the Future Comprehensive Plan.

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner Word of Life Christian Church, Inc. and applicant Vicki Jones request a major S-1 (Special) plan 
revision for property located at 6389 Washington Road, Tax M ap 024 Parcel  ID 065, 6.93 +/- acres, 
and currently zoned S-1 (Special). The applicant is requesting the major revision for a proposed multi-
purpose building. A revised narrative and plan is included with the request.   
 
The subject propert y is located on the north side of Washington Road, opposite the intersection of 
Eubank Drive and Washington Road. All adjacent properties to the north, east, and west on the same 
side of Washington Road are zoned R -4 (Recreational Residential) . Properties to the south  on the 
opposite side of Washington Road are zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural). The subject property was 
rezoned in 2020 (RZ20- 10-01). That application proposed a 8,750 square foot multi -purpose building 
and additional gazebos  and was approved with conditions by the Board of Commissioners. The  
property was then the subject of a major  revision in 2024 (RZ24-06-03) which removed the proposed 
multi-purpose building, instead proposing an addition to the existing church building and parking lot 
expansions. That application was also approved with conditions.   
 
The proposed revision maintains the elements of the 2024 major revision: an expansion of the parking 
lot along Washington Road, a future building addition, and one or more open-air pavilions or gazebos 
near the recreational pond; but adds a proposed multi -purpose building on the western side of the 
ingress/egress driveway where there is an existing structure currently. The proposed paved parking lot 
expansion shows a total of 28 spaces built as a continuation of the existing parking lot along 
Washington Road. A landscape strip is shown but it is noted that the specific design will be coordinated 
during site plan review. This was anticipated with the previous request, so staff is in agreement  to 
continue to apply that method to this revision. The proposed building expansion is not expected to 
exceed 4,000 square feet (the existing overall building is approximately 8,000 square feet in size). The 
narrative notes that the future building expansi on will be finished with materials to match the existing 
church building with final details to be coordinated with the Planning Department for review when the

architectural plans are developed. The concept plan shows where proposed pavilions or gazebos may 
be located on the site. The proposed multi-purpose building’s dimensions and total square footage are 
unknown currently. The concept plan shows its general location, and the narrative indicates that it is 
not expected it will exceed 8,750 square feet. Buffers are to remain as shown, including encroachments 
at the rear of the site. Generally, the setbacks remain the same as the previous applications. The 2020 
rezoning established a minimum 20-foot setback from the existing water main along Washington Road 
and a 15-foot setback from the front lot line for the proposed multi -purpose building at that time. The 
2024 concept plan without a multi -purpose building showed the existing building on the front of the 
property does encroach into the 125’ building setback. The currently proposed multi -purpose building 
will comply with the setbacks outlined by the 2020 approval. This will be addressed with a proposed 
condition for clarity.  
   
Staff is generally in support of the request. Buffers are established and there are no existing residences 
adjacent to the property, so it is unlikely that these structures will impact any nearby property. The 
building addition is at the rear of the existing church, so it is unlikely to cause any concern with that 
location. Staff has no concerns about the proposed gazebos or pavilions that may be placed on the 
property.  
 
This is likely the only realistic location for a parking expansion due to the topography on the site and 
location of other structures. Staff is amenable to working with the applicant on the landscape plan to 
accomplish the code requirement with an alternate plan. The situation with the proposed multi-purpose 
structure is similar. This is likely the only realistic location for such a structure considering topography 
and existing structures. L andscaping is planned and illustrated on the concept plan between the 
building and the front lot line to soften its visual impact. Staff is generally comfortable with its proposed 
location. However, the Health Department’s submitted comments explain that, if the new building 
cannot connect to the existing septic system on the site, a level 3 soil survey will be required for any 
newly proposed system to serve the new building. 
 
The Fire Marshal and Fire Department have identified some concerns  with the proposed site layout. 
According to their comments, drive aisle widths and vehicle turnarounds at the ends of the parking 
areas do not appear adequate to provide access for emergency vehicles. A fire hydrant will likely be 
required for the site, and there may not be sufficient access to all portions of the proposed building for 
fire rescue equipment and personnel. The project ’s engineer has been made aware of the concerns 
from both fire and the Health Department and has expressed confidence that the issues can be 
resolved during site plan review. Therefore, the current proposed concept plan is acceptable for this 
major revision stage of the development process. 
 
Regarding conditions, as noted above, the existing building is within the front setback. According to the 
supplied concept plan, the building is approximately 15 feet from the front property line. Staff proposes 
a condition carrying over the setback requirement from the 2020 application for a 15-foot front setback 
from the lot line with the caveat that the front setback be reduced only for the currently proposed 
building. Beyond that, s taff has no concerns with the building at that location given the provided 
condition is met and the illustrated landscaping is installed.  
 
Regarding Foundations for the Future, the subject parcel is located within the Rural 
Residential/Agricultural Character Area on the Character Area map. The Rural Residential/Agricultural 
Character Area consists of large- lot single family homes and parcels with agricultural activities. It

agricultural economy, scenic character, and open space network, and may include supporting 
neighborhood-scale commercial, service, and civic uses. Future development will continue to reinforce 
the existing sense of openness and separation between homes, preserving the character that defines 
these neighborhoods. Places of worship are anticipated civic uses to serve the surrounding 
communities in this character area. The church has been there for several years already, and the 
proposed expansions on the church campus will permit a use that is suitable in view of Foundations for

Due to the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends approval with condition of the requested 
major S-1 (Special) plan revision for property located at 6389 Washington Road, Tax Map 024 Parcel

ITEM: Acknowledgment of the Financial Sublease Agreement between the AU Medical Center, Inc. and the 
Hospital Authority of Columbia County 
  
BACKGROUND: These documents put in place the hospital leasing arrangements contemplated by the 
2023 development agreement. The Hospital Authority signs two agreements, and the County signs a 
limited acknowledgment. AU Medical Center, Inc., which is part of Wellstar, remains responsible for 
operating the hospital. 
Hospital Authority 
•    Financing Sublease: AU Medical Center leases the hospital premises to the Authority. This gives the 
Authority a leasehold interest in the hospital as part of the financing arrangement. The Authority pays a 
one-time rent of $10. 
•    Operating Sublease: The Authority leases the hospital premises back to AU Medical Center to operate. 
This agreement places responsibility on AU Medical Center for hospital operations and payment of the 
hospital financing obligations. It also includes commitments concerning emergency services, indigent care, 
financial reporting, and Authority representation on AU Medical Center’s board. 
Why two leases? One gives the Authority its interest in the hospital for the financing arrangement; the other 
places the hospital’s operation and related payment responsibilities with AU Medical Center. 
County 
•    Acknowledgment by Wellstar and the County: The County acknowledges its right to receive notice if the 
Authority defaults under the Financing Sublease and an opportunity to correct that default. Correcting the 
default is optional under this provision. The acknowledgment itself does not create a new payment 
guarantee or eliminate the County’s existing financing commitments. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff Recommends that the Board acknowledge the Financial Sublease 
Agreement between AU Medical Center, Inc. and the Hospital Authority of Columbia County.

ITEM: Community Rating System (CRS) Re-Certification and Hazard Mitigation Stormwater Presentation 
  
BACKGROUND: Location – N/A 
 
Request – N/A. Information purposes only to meet CRS Program Requirements.  
 
History – The CRS program is voluntary and awards points for proactive flood-related activities that 
produce a more flood-ready and flood-resilient community. In exchange for committing to various flood-
ready activities conducted by the County, residents are awarded with a discount on their flood insurance 
policy. Currently, Columbia County citizens receive a 20% discount on their flood insurance policies.  
Part of the annual CRS recertification is an update on two activities (Program for Public Information and 
Repetitive Loss Area Analysis) in addition to a presentation on a third activity (Flood Hazard Mitigation). 
Program for Public Information: 
• This program continues to reach a variety of target audiences in the community through social 
media, mailing, newsletters, and presentations.  
• During the past year, we continued providing updates to outreach covering both information and 
availability. Additionally, new outreach material on flood/emergency preparedness and floodplain 
function was created and is available on the County website. 
• The County would like to recognize and thank the committee efforts of Robbie Moore, Blanchard & 
Calhoun Insurance Agency, Inc.; Jamie Pierce, Pinnacle Bank; Caleb Willing, Better Homes & 
Gardens Real Estate; and Cassidy Harris, Columbia County Public Relations Manager.  
 
Repetitive Loss Area Analysis: 
• This program continues to provide educational materials and support for properties that have had 
multiple flood insurance claims. Every one of these properties was field inspected by staff to 
determine if conditions were present to support eligibility for the Emergency Watershed Protection 
Program grant with the Natural Resources Conservation Services (NRCS). Several properties were 
eligible, and all received NRCS approval and funding for vegetative debris clean-up from their 
nearby waterway. This grant was completed in fall 2025 and all approved properties received 
cleanup to remove Hurricane Helene-generated debris from waterways present on the property. 
This grant serves to protect life and property from additional flooding and soil erosion. 
• During the past year, we continued providing outreach to promote flood insurance purchase for 
structures in all zones of risk, to include zone X/low-risk.  
 
Flood Hazard Mitigation Plan (Plan): 
• This program continues to prioritize infrastructure projects to help minimize the potential of flood 
related hazards and streambank erosion. 
• Stormwater Operations completed three large projects from the Plan to resolve infrastructure issues 
at Hidden Place, RiverShyre Drive, and Ashridge Way in addition to conducting thousands of 
inspections to further identify maintenance, repair, and/or replacement needs within the County 
stormwater infrastructure system. All of this work was completed within the last 12 months, utilizing 
the Stormwater Utility Fee and SPLOST Fund.  
 
Since Columbia County’s participation in the CRS, the program required a signature on an annual 
recertification form, or we underwent a full audit to confirm that various activities continue to be performed 
in such a manner as to satisfy the requirements of the CRS. This year the CRS is not requiring those steps, 
only that the County continues to meet all activities in the approved program. Staff confirms all 
requirements continue to be met and appreciates County leadership support of this program.

533060.

ITEM: Independent Contractor Agreement with Infrastructure Systems Management, LLC (ISM)  for 
Professional Engineering Services for the Range Road Facilities Water & Sewer Improvements 
  
BACKGROUND: An Independent Contractor Agreement with ISM for Professional Engineering Services 
for Water and Sewer Improvements at the Range Road Facilities. The scope of this project includes the 
design and installation of an area lift station, gravity sanitary sewer system, and building service 
connections to accommodate both current and future planned facilities. The project also includes the 
creation of a looped water line system along Range Road to enhance overall water flow and system 
performance for the area. 
The engineering fee is calculated at 7% of the estimated construction cost of $1,250,622.00, resulting in a 
fee of $87,543.54. Funding for this expenditure will be allocated from the Extension and Renewal budget, 
code 57037-25-015-700. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends the approval of this agreement.

ITEM: Payment to Blair Construction for Emergency Shoring on Oakley Pirkle Rd 
  
BACKGROUND: LOCATION: Oakley Pirkle Rd at the Crawford Creek Crossing 
  
REQUEST: Payment to Blair Construction for emergency shoring on Oakley Pirkle Rd 
  
HISTORY: On September 2, 2026, County staff identified a failed wing wall at the Crawford Creek box 
culvert beneath Oakley Pirkle Rd. The failure exposed several utilities, including a 10-inch water main, and 
compromised the adjacent roadway embankment. 
 
The County Engineer, in coordination with Roads & Bridges, Water Utility, and Road Construction staff, 
determined that immediate shoring was necessary to protect the exposed utilities, maintain roadway 
stability, and protect the traveling public. Due to the culvert size, steep slopes, limited right-of-way, and 
need for specialized shoring, the work could not be safely performed by County forces. 
 
With County Management’s concurrence, Blair Construction, a registered County vendor, was engaged to 
complete the emergency shoring, including installation of sheet-pile shoring. The County Engineer issued a 
notice to proceed once the scope, schedule, and cost of work were agreed to. 
 
Policy 603.1 authorizes suspension of formal bidding procedures during emergencies affecting public 
health, safety, welfare, or essential governmental services. Pursuant to OCGA § 36-91-22, the Board of 
Commissioners must ratify emergency public works as soon as practicable. 
 
FUNDING: $325,517.00 (50% TIA Discretionary; 50% Stormwater Infrastructure Fund) 
  
TIMELINE: Notification of the wing wall failure was received on September 02, 2026. The emergency 
shoring work was completed on October 02, 2026. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends payment to Blair Construction for emergency shoring on 
Oakley Pirkle Rd

BACKGROUND: Location -  4065 Columbia Road, Martinez, Ga 30907

History - Columbia County acquired the property, including the former bank building, in connection with the 
Flowing Wells Road Widening Project. Now that the roadway project is complete, staff has been evaluating 
whether to surplus and sell the property or whether to demolish the existing structure and redevelop the site

ITEM: Resolution 26-26 Concerning a Determination to Abandon and sell a portion of Crawford Place 
Lane. 
  
BACKGROUND:  
Location - The section of Crawford Place Lane and Right-of-Way which is a curve that connects both 
straight sections of “Tract 1 Local Road” and “Tract 3 Local Road” as shown more specifically on the 
attached plat dated 6/18/2026, and labeled "Tract 2 Local Road." 
 
Request - Approve this second and final Resolution 26-26 to abandon and sell a Portion of Crawford 
Place Lane. 
 
History – Quit claimed in 2008 to continue the access road behind North Columbia Elementary 
School. The elementary school has since been demolished, and the road is no longer needed. 
  
Funding - No funding required.  
  
Timeline - Upon adoption, the property will be sold according to state law. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION:  
Staff recommends approval of this second and final Resolution 26-26 to abandon and sell a portion of 
Crawford Place Lane. 
  
COMMITTEE COMMENTS:  
  
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION / MOTION:  
 
RESOLUTION NUMBER 26-26 
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS 
OF COLUMBIA COUNTY, GEORGIA CONCERNING A DETERMINATION TO ABANDON 
AND SELL A PORTION OF CRAWFORD PLACE LANE LABELED  
TRACT 2 ON THE ATTACHED PLAT 
 THIS RESOLUTION adopted by the Board of Commissioners of Columbia County. 
 
WHEREAS, it has been proposed that the Board of Commissioners of Columbia County, 
(“Board”)  make a determination whether it is in the best interest of the public for a portion of the right-of-
way/old roadbed of Crawford Place Lane from a certain point approximately 950 feet from Crawford Place 
Road and approximately 1,050 feet from Ray Owens Road, its dimensions resembling that of a triangle, 
hereinafter the “Property,” as shown more particularly on the attached plat dated 06/18/2026, and labeled 
“Tract 2 Local Road”, a copy of which is attached hereto as “Crawford Place Lane,” to be abandoned by 
Columbia County for public right-of-way purposes and sold according to state law. 
 
 WHEREAS, the Board examined the issue of abandonment of the Property and by Resolution 26-
21 adopted on October 6, 2026 (the “Resolution”), set forth requirements in order to properly accomplish 
the abandonment;  
 
 WHEREAS, pursuant to the Resolution, a public hearing was held before the Public Works and 
Engineering Services Committee, on October 27, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. in the Building A auditorium of the 
Columbia County Government Center at 630 Ronald Reagan Drive Evans, Georgia;  
 
 WHEREAS, a notice of such public hearing was published on October 7, 2026 and October 14, 
2026 in the Augusta Chronicle, the newspaper in which the Legal Notices of Columbia County are 
published.  
 
 WHEREAS, following the public meeting, the Public Works and Engineering Services Committee 
Chairman reported to the Board that no party in attendance objected to the abandonment;  
  
 WHEREAS, the County determined that it would serve the public’s best interest to abandon the 
property; 
 
 NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved by, and with the authority of, the Board: 
1. The right-of-way on the Property shall be abandoned by the County. 
2. The right-of-way on the Property shall be sold according to state law.  
3. This Resolution shall become effective immediately upon its adoption. 
 
Adopted November 3, 2026.

ITEM: Acknowledgment of the Financial Sublease Agreement between the AU Medical Center, Inc. and the 
Hospital Authority of Columbia County 
  
BACKGROUND: These documents put in place the hospital leasing arrangements contemplated by the 
2023 development agreement. The Hospital Authority signs two agreements, and the County signs a 
limited acknowledgment. AU Medical Center, Inc., which is part of Wellstar, remains responsible for 
operating the hospital. 
Hospital Authority 
•    Financing Sublease: AU Medical Center leases the hospital premises to the Authority. This gives the 
Authority a leasehold interest in the hospital as part of the financing arrangement. The Authority pays a 
one-time rent of $10. 
•    Operating Sublease: The Authority leases the hospital premises back to AU Medical Center to operate. 
This agreement places responsibility on AU Medical Center for hospital operations and payment of the 
hospital financing obligations. It also includes commitments concerning emergency services, indigent care, 
financial reporting, and Authority representation on AU Medical Center’s board. 
Why two leases? One gives the Authority its interest in the hospital for the financing arrangement; the other 
places the hospital’s operation and related payment responsibilities with AU Medical Center. 
County 
•    Acknowledgment by Wellstar and the County: The County acknowledges its right to receive notice if the 
Authority defaults under the Financing Sublease and an opportunity to correct that default. Correcting the 
default is optional under this provision. The acknowledgment itself does not create a new payment 
guarantee or eliminate the County’s existing financing commitments. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff Recommends that the Board acknowledge the Financial Sublease 
Agreement between AU Medical Center, Inc. and the Hospital Authority of Columbia County. 
  
COMMITTEE COMMENTS: Forward to Consent Agenda. 
  
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION / MOTION: Approved acknowledging the Financial Sublease 
Agreement between AU Medical Center, Inc. and the Hospital Authority of Columbia County.

ITEM: Payment to Blair Construction for Emergency Shoring on Oakley Pirkle Rd 
  
BACKGROUND: LOCATION: Oakley Pirkle Rd at the Crawford Creek Crossing 
  
REQUEST: Payment to Blair Construction for emergency shoring on Oakley Pirkle Rd 
  
HISTORY: On September 2, 2026, County staff identified a failed wing wall at the Crawford Creek box 
culvert beneath Oakley Pirkle Rd. The failure exposed several utilities, including a 10-inch water main, and 
compromised the adjacent roadway embankment. 
 
The County Engineer, in coordination with Roads & Bridges, Water Utility, and Road Construction staff, 
determined that immediate shoring was necessary to protect the exposed utilities, maintain roadway 
stability, and protect the traveling public. Due to the culvert size, steep slopes, limited right-of-way, and 
need for specialized shoring, the work could not be safely performed by County forces. 
 
With County Management’s concurrence, Blair Construction, a registered County vendor, was engaged to 
complete the emergency shoring, including installation of sheet-pile shoring. The County Engineer issued a 
notice to proceed once the scope, schedule, and cost of work were agreed to. 
 
Policy 603.1 authorizes suspension of formal bidding procedures during emergencies affecting public 
health, safety, welfare, or essential governmental services. Pursuant to OCGA § 36-91-22, the Board of 
Commissioners must ratify emergency public works as soon as practicable. 
 
FUNDING: $325,517.00 (50% TIA Discretionary; 50% Stormwater Infrastructure Fund) 
  
TIMELINE: Notification of the wing wall failure was received on September 02, 2026. The emergency 
shoring work was completed on October 02, 2026.
