ITEM: VA26-09-01, Variance to Section 90-147(g)(10)(b)(2)(v) Use Provisions, 5549 Columbia Road, Tax 
Map 050 Parcel 002K, 2.65 +/- acres, and currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial) - Postponed 
from the September 15, 2026 meeting. 
  
BACKGROUND: See attached Staff Report- VA26-09-01 
 
Planning Commission Date: September 3rd, 2026 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends to disapprove the request for a variance to Section 90-
147(g)(10)(b) Use Provisions for the property located at 5549 Columbia Road, Tax Map 050 
Parcel ID 002K, 2.65 +/- acres, and currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial) to permit 24-hour 
operation. 
  
COMMITTEE COMMENTS: Planning Commission: No comments.  
 
Applicant, Heather McBride, 2550 W Tyvola Rd, Charlotte, NC, stated that Circle K is a 24hr brand. The 
surrounding parcels are not residential and could include 24 hour quick service restaurants. They will have 
the proper staff, lighting and security system to ensure the public’s safety.    
 
Cathy Richards, 1044 Kalmia Circle, stated her and her family use the greenway often. She is against the 
24 hour gas station and is unsure how the traffic would even flow properly out of this parcel. Is also 
concerned about the light population this will cause. This area is not being developed with the mindset to 
protect our natural environment or the health of our citizens.  
 
Marlena Bergeron, 2545 Willow Creek Ct, stated she is against the 24 hour operation. There is already a 
gas station down the street. She stated that things we protect are the things we love and that the Planning 
Commission supports franchise owners and business that aren’t owned locally. Believes that the landowner 
has more power and they live out of state than those who live in the area. She is worried about the traffic 
pattern this will cause and if a pedestrian activated button would be installed. She would like Planning staff 
and Commissioners to review the window of time when a property is rezoned, and if they haven’t started 
developing within a certain time frame then they should have to revert to the previous zoning.   
 
Beth Connell, 2538 Falling Branch Lane, stated she is also against the 24 hour operation. She is not 
against development but opposed to poorly planned developments. Believes that a community crossroads 
should be different from every other intersection.   
 
Dan Lanning, 825 Rolling Brook Lane, states that he drives by this location daily. This location right now 
isn’t a 24-hour area. If someone needs to get gas they can get gas by the interstate. Believe that the 
applicants can come back in 2-4 years and ask for the 24-hour operation if this area is deemed that.   
 
For further explanation on committee comments, please see the excerpt from the September 3rd, 2026 
Planning Commission meeting. 
 
Vice-Chairman Holloway made a motion to recommend disapproval of VA26-09-01, Variance to Section 90-
147(g)(10)(b)(2)(v) Use Provisions, 5549 Columbia Road, Tax Map 050 Parcel 002K, 2.65 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial). Commissioner Cato seconded the motion.  
 
Motion Carried: 5-0 
  
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION / MOTION: I make a motion to disapprove the request for the variance 
to section 90-147 for property located at tax map 050 parcel 002k to permit 24 hour operation.

The following is a draft of the actions taken at the September 3rd, 2026 Columbia County 
Planning Commission meeting. This document has not been reviewed or approved by the 
Planning Commission and is not an official record of the meeting. The Planning Commission 
will approve the official minutes on September 17th, 2026. 
 
(H1b6) VA26-09-01, Variance to Section 90-147(g)(10)(b)(2)(v) Use Provisions, 5549 Columbia 
Road, Tax Map 050 Parcel 002K, 2.65 +/- acres, and currently zoned C-C (Community 
Commercial). 
 
Staff Member Dylan Douglas presented the staff recommendation. 
 
Chairman Moody opened the public hearing at 7:30PM. 
 
Applicant, Heather McBride, 2550 W Tyvola Rd, Charlotte, NC, stated that Circle K is a 24hr brand. 
The surrounding parcels are not residential and could include 24 hour quick service restaurants. 
They will have the proper staff, lighting and security system to ensure the public’s safety.   
 
Cathy Richards, 1044 Kalmia Circle, stated her and her family use the greenway often. She is 
against the 24 hour gas station and is unsure how the traffic would even flow properly out of this 
parcel. Is also concerned about the light population this will cause. This area is not being developed 
with the mindset to protect our natural environment or the health of our citizens. 
 
Marlena Bergeron, 2545 Willow Creek Ct, stated she is against the 24 hour operation. There is 
already a gas station down the street. She stated that things we protect are the things we love and 
that the Planning Commission supports franchise owners and business that aren’t owned locally. 
Believes that the landowner has more power and they live out of state than those who live in the 
area. She is worried about the traffic pattern this will cause and if a pedestrian activated button 
would be installed. She would like Planning staff and Commissioners to review the window of time 
when a property is rezoned, and if they haven’t started developing within a certain time frame then 
they should have to revert to the previous zoning.  
 
Beth Connell, 2538 Falling Branch Lane, stated she is also against the 24 hour operation. She is not 
against development but opposed to poorly planned developments. Believes that a community 
crossroads should be different from every other intersection.  
 
Dan Lanning, 825 Rolling Brook Lane, states that he drives by this location daily. This location right 
now isn’t a 24 hour area. If someone needs to get gas they can get gas by the interstate. Believe 
that the applicants can come back in 2-4 years and ask for the 24 hour operation if this area is 
deemed that.  
 
Chairman Moody closed the public hearing at 7:48 PM. 
 
Vice-Chairman Holloway made a motion to recommend disapproval of VA26-09-01, Variance to 
Section 90-147(g)(10)(b)(2)(v) Use Provisions, 5549 Columbia Road, Tax Map 050 Parcel 002K, 
2.65 +/- acres, and currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial).Commissioner Cato seconded 
the motion. The motion carried unanimously.

Summary and Recommendation 
O
wner MHR Landlord Evans, LLC and applicant Circle K Stores, Inc. request a variance to Section 90-
147(g)(10)(b) Use Provisions for the property located at 5549 Columbia Road, Tax Map 050 Parcel ID 
002K, 2.65 +/- acres, and currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial). The applicant is requesting 
the variance to permit 24-hour operation of a proposed convenience store. Provided with the application 
is an addendum explaining the rationale for the request.    
The s
ubject parcel is located on the northeast corner of the intersection of Columbia Road and William 
Few Parkway. Properties to the north and east are also zoned C-C (Community Commercial) as a part 
of the same eventual overall commercial development. The very large parcel a cross William Few 
Parkway is split zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural), S-1 (Special) for the Martin Marietta quarry, M-2 
(General Industrial) for an asphalt plant, and C -C with the portion of property zoned C -C immediately 
across from the subject parcel of this request. Property to the south across Columbia Road is zoned S-
1 for a proposed funeral home but is currently still undeveloped. Property on the southwest corner of 
the intersection of William Few and Columbia is zoned S-1 for the Columbia County fairgrounds. 
A
s noted, the applicant is requesting to permit a proposed convenience store to be open 24 hours a 
day. Per Section 90-147 (g)(10)(b) Use Provisions, the hours of operation for a convenience store with 
gas pumps are from 6AM to 11PM. Per the provided addendum, the applicant has noted that the 
variance for 24-hour operation is necessary for the convenience store and fuel pumps to be available 
to county residents at any time of day. They explain that 24-hour operation is standard across Circle K 
stores. The applicant also contends that granting the variances would not negatively impact the 
adjacent properties as they are all commercially zoned or in similar commercial use. Specifically, they 
reference that the broader Patriot’s Square Commercial Development will build out with other 
commercial uses that are all allowed to operate 24 hours a day. In that scenario, the convenience store 
would be the only use subject to operating hour restrictions. After consulting with staff prior to applying

for this request, the applicants have included a photometric plan with their application packet to address 
any concerns there might be with their plan related to lighting. 
 
Additionally, this site also features stretches of the Columbia County greenway along both of its road 
frontages. This being the case, Columbia County has already taken great care to review and approve 
a landscaping plan for the overall Patriot’s Square development. The applicants, again in consultation 
with staff, are aware of this landscape plan and were provided a copy of it prior to submitting this 
request. They included the relevant portions of that plan for their specific site with this application 
submittal and have communicated that they are comfortable and prepared to comply with or augment 
that approved landscaping plan where needed. 
 
Staff would generally disagree with the applicants’ opinion that the limitation on operating hours would 
produce a hardship. There are many other convenience stores in the county that operate according to 
this provision without issue. The residents near those locations also presumably are sufficiently served 
by those convenience stores during their current operating hours or, at least, have adjusted to those 
hours to serve their needs. It is also very unlikely that the many, if any, of the other commercial 
businesses that will populate Patriot’s Square will operate 24 -hours-a-day even if they are allowed to. 
For some examples, uses like grocery stores, restaurants, day cares, and other retail providers are 
common in commercial developments and rarely operate 24 hours. 
 
Generally, approval of request s for 24-hour operation of convenience stores  have been restricted to 
locations within close proximity of Interstate-20.  One example of this kind of approval occurred in 2022 
for 4311 Wrightsboro Road as the subject of VA22- 08-01. This parcel is roughly half a mile from an I -
20 interchange and has multiple convenience stores between it and the interchange that predate this 
ordinance and, therefore, already operate 24- hours-a-day. That applicant also had some exceptional 
issues with theft and burglary they sought to combat by extending their operating hours.  Another 
approval was granted in 2023 for 925 Husk Box Way via RZ23-04-03. This site is roughly one-tenth of 
a mile from I -20 and is surrounded by at least a couple layers of dense commercial development. In 
2024, VA24- 06-04 approved 24 -hour operation for 4099 Jimmie Dyess Parkway, a parcel on an 
immediately adjacent corner to an I -20 exit. The subject location of this current request , however, is 
roughly over 3  miles from the nearest interstate interchange.  While the parcel’s frontages along 2 
arterial roadways are likely to drive high-demand during the code compliant operating hours of 6AM to 
11PM, it is unlikely they will produce 24-hour traffic to the business like Interstate-20 does. 
 
The only exception to this trend was for 6697 Washington Road in 2021 via VA21- 03-02. This 
convenience store is in the northernmost reaches of the county near the lake front and had already 
been operating roughly from 5:30AM until midnight prior to the int roduction of the provision impacting 
operating hours. Those applicants were seeking to continue serving the fishing community who are 
often on the lake before the sun rises. One aspect of that application also sought to broaden the 
business’ services to include bait sales in those early hours. Due to this unique location and service to 
the public, this request ultimately received approval  with an added stipulation restricting deliveries for 
the business to between 6AM and 11PM.  
 
The most pertinent application for this one, though, occurred directly across William Few Parkway from 
this site. The C-C (Community Commercial) portion of that parcel was rezoned in 2024 as the subject 
of file RZ24- 06-07 for an intended convenience store construction. That rezoning application had an 
accompanying variance application for a couple site layout requirements and, originally, seeking 24-

hour operation. However, the applicants ultimately chose to withdraw the aspect of their variance 
request for 24-hour operation. The rezoning and the remainder of the variance requests were ultimately 
approved. However, construction on that site has not begun.  
 
Since the introduction of the use provision limiting convenience store operating hours in 2016, 6697 
Washington Road is the only location not in proximity to the interstate that has been granted a variance 
to its requirements and is an exceptional case. Approval of this request would not serve a need for the 
overall public or surrounding area, and denial of the request would not produce any undue or 
exceptional hardship. 
 
Due to the reasoning outlined above, s taff recommends to disapprove the request for a variance to 
Section 90-147(g)(10)(b) Use Provisions for the property located at 5549 Columbia Road, Tax Map 050 
Parcel ID 002K, 2.65 +/- acres, and currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial) to permit 24 -hour 
operation.

Criteria for Evaluation of Variance Proposal 
 
1. There are special circumstances or conditions unique to the property that do not 
generally apply to the district.  
The property has frontages along William Few Parkway and Columbia Road, two arterial roads. 
This site also features stretches of the Columbia County greenway along both of those  road 
frontages.  
 
2. The special circumstances or conditions are such that the strict application of the 
provisions of this chapter would deprive the applicant of any reasonable use of his land. 
Mere loss of value shall not justify a variance. There must be a deprivation of beneficial 
use of land.  
The applicant c an use the property for a convenience store subject to the limitations on 
operating hours as is. William Few Parkway and Columbia Road are arterial roadways and will 
presumably produce high demand during code compliant operating hours . They are not 
interstates, though, so it is unlikely they would drive enough demand between 11PM and 6AM 
to warrant approval of this 24-hour operation request.

Summary and Recommendation 
O
wner Andrea W. Timmerman and applicant Eric W. Clark request a rezoning from a split zoned P -1 
(Professional) and C-2 (General Commercial) to P- 1 (Professional) for property located at 436 Furys 
Ferry Road, Tax Map 082A Parcel 059B, 0.3 +/ - acres. The property is currently zoned P -1 and C -2 
and is located with in the Furys Ferry Corridor Protection Overlay District. While the property could 
certainly be used as currently zoned, having a parcel zoned with one zoning classification is simpler for 
both Columbia County and the property owner to address the development of that parcel. The applicant 
has included a concept  plan showing the proposed building additions to the current dental office. A 
companion variance relating to building setbacks and buffers has also been applied for under VA26-
10-01.
The s
ubject property is located on the west side of Furys Ferry Road. The parcels to the west, 1106 
Furys Lane and the retention pond are also split zoned P -1 and C -2 as per files RZ86 -03-03A and 
RZ86-03-03 respectively. When this rezoning action was taken in 1986, the P -1 zoning was meant to 
act as a separation between the residential area to the north and the C -2 zoning. Other properties to 
the south are zoned C-2. Surrounding properties to the north are zoned R-3 (Single Family Residential) 
and are part of the Wexford Subdivision. Properties across Furys Ferry Road are zoned C-2.  
P
er the provided concept plan, the applicant proposes to build two additions to the current dental office. 
One addition is planned along the elevation facing the residence to the north. The second  addition is 
planned along the elevation facing Furys Lane. With the building expansions being restricted to the 
grassed areas on site, the existing parking spaces will not be impacted and no changes are proposed. 
With the increase in floor area, the office will still meet the parking standards required by code.  
Ther
e is an old, deteriorated wooden fence that is on the shared property line with the adjacent 
residence that will be removed and replaced as a part of the proposed site work. Planning staff have

Overall, staff have no major concerns with this request. The Fire Marshal has included a comment that

expansion is currently at a preliminary design stage and the site design will be addressed by the 
applicant’s Engineer at the Plan Review stage of the project and reviewed by County staff.  
 
The subject property is within the Community Commercial Character Area and a Commercial Corridor 
on the Foundations for the Future Development Map. This character area consists of medium to large 
concentrations of retail and services that draw customers from nearby neighborhoods, generally at key 
intersections of higher -traffic streets. These areas are intended to provide daily needs and specialty 
goods in multi-tenant centers and outparcels. These character areas should continue to include a mix 
of local and national retailers, restaurants, professional and personal services, and public gathering 
spaces along commercial corridors and at designated nodes to serve nearby residents.  
 
Furys Ferry Road is also one of the commercial corridor s, which play s a key role in shaping how 
residents, visitors, and future investors perceive the area, offer  a range of uses including shopping 
centers, gas stations, fast -food restaurants, and industrial facilities. Most of Columbia County’s 
economic activity is concentrated along several major corridors, including I -20, Washington Road, 
Columbia Road, Riverwatch Parkway, Evans to Locks Road, Belair Road, and Furys Ferry Road. Furys 
Ferry Road has seen improvements with landscaped medians , street trees and sidewalks creating a 
more attractive corridor. The use as a dental office is not changing and is compatible with the purpose 
and intent of the Foundations for the Future Comprehensive Plan.  
   
Due to the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends approval of the rezoning from a split zoned P-
1 (Professional) and C-2 (General Commercial) to P-1 (Professional) for property located at 436 Furys 
Ferry Road, Tax Map 082A Parcel 059B, 0.3 +/- acres for professional office use.

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner Andrea W. Timmerman and applicant Eric W. Clark request a variance to Sections 90 -98 List 
of lot & structure requirements and 90-139 Buffers & screening for property located at 436 Furys Ferry 
Road, Tax Map 082A Parcel 059B, 0.3 +/- acres, and currently split zoned P-1 (Professional) and C-2 
(General Commercial). The applicant is requesting the variance to reduce the building setbacks and to 
reduce the buffer against residential property to allow proposed additions to the existing building.  A 
companion rezoning has also been applied for under RZ26- 10-04 as having a parcel zoned with one 
zoning classification is simpler for both Columbia County and the property owner to address the 
development of that parcel. The applicant has included a concept plan showing the proposed building 
additions to the current dental office and an addendum explaining the variances.  
 
The subject property is located on the west side of Furys Ferry Road. The parcels to the west, 1106 
Furys Lane and the retention pond are also split zoned P -1 and C -2 as per files RZ86 -03-03A and 
RZ86-03-03 respectively. When this rezoning action was taken in 1986, the P -1 zoning was meant to 
act as a separation between the residential area to the north and the C -2 zoning. Other properties to 
the south are zoned C-2. Surrounding properties to the north are zoned R-3 (Single Family Residential) 
and are part of the Wexford Subdivision. Properties across Furys Ferry Road are zoned C-2.  
 
Per the provided concept plan, the applicant proposes to build two additions to the current dental office. 
One addition is planned along the elevation facing the residence to the north and wraps around the 
corner to the west.  The second addition is planned along the elevation facing Furys Lane. With the 
building expansions being restricted to the grassed areas on site, the existing parking spaces will not 
be impacted and no changes are proposed. With the increase in floor area of approximately 620 square 
feet, for an additional doctor’s office and two treatment rooms, totaling two doctors’ offices and six 
treatment rooms, the office will still meet the minimum parking standards required by code.

In addition, the provided plan shows that the existing office building encroaches approximately 5 feet 
into the 20-foot structural buffer required by current code against the residential property to the north 
located at 3710 Wexford Place S, so the building is currently non-conforming. The plan also shows that 
the existing covered porch area with steps to the west encroaches approximately 5 feet into the 10-foot 
side required setback. The variance request, if approved, would remedy this non-compliance.  
 
The proposed addition to the north will require a buffer reduction to 10 feet from the north property line 
to allow the building expansion. The side setback requirement in the code is 10 feet but as the buffer 
requirement is 20 feet, this is the more restrictive item . This addition wraps around the corner to the 
west and will require a setback reduction from 10 feet to 5 feet from the west property line. The second 
building addition is located to the south and it will require a setback reduction from 55 feet from the 
centerline of Furys Lane to 50 feet. This is shown as 35 feet on the concept plan as it is measured from 
the front property line. The front setback from Furys Ferry Road is required to be 125 feet and this is in 
compliance and no changes are proposed for that side.  
 
The plat shows a 10 -foot drainage and utility easement along the north property line and a 5- foot 
drainage and utility easement along the west property line. There is 10 -foot utility easement along the 
south property line. None of the additions will impact the easements so no encroachment agreements 
are necessary for this project to move forward. The current office meets the architectural requirements 
of the Corridor Protection Overlay District  and the new additions will be  planned to match the current 
architecture.  
 
Staff does have some concerns with the request  related to site design.  The existing use is being 
increased in gross floor area by more than 25 percent and the code requires that the site shall conform 
to the landscaping and screening requirements of the code.  The site has a significant grade change 
from the east to the west property lines and this is not necessarily unique to this property since the 
other commercial lots also either have a slope or a retaining wall and abut residential properties. The 
parking lot along the Furys Ferry Road frontage is on the higher portion of the site and there is a 
concrete flume that channels the stormwater  from the parking lot into the swale along the  northern 
property line. This swale is located within the buffer area and there are currently no trees along that 
side. It is noted that the site area between the office and the residential property to the north is fairly 
limited and the addition reduces this area further.  
 
There is an old, deteriorated wooden fence that is on the shared property line with the adjacent 
residence that will be removed and replaced as a part of the proposed site work. Planning staff have 
spoken with the neighbor who has agreed to the removal of the fence and supports the installation of 
the new fence. A condition has been added stating that the structural buffer is reduced to 10 feet from 
the north property line and the existing fence will be replaced with a new 6 foot high wood or vinyl 
privacy fence providing a finished appearance on both sides of the fence.  
 
The neighbor also raised some concerns about stormwater and was reassured that engineered plans 
would be required for County review prior to the issuance of site and building permits for the building 
expansion. If the variance request is approved, the next step will be the engineered plan submittal to 
the Plan Review Department and that will address any technical concerns. The Fire Marshal has 
included a comment that there does not appear to be an existing fire hydrant within the distance 
required by code. The building expansion is currently at a preliminary design stage and the site design

The dental office was built in 1995 and a new engineered site plan to address site issues will help

Summary and Recommendation 
Owners Chad and Stacy Fowers and applicant Stacy Fowers  request a Provisional Home Occupation 
for Tax Map 002 Parcel 014, 9 +/- acres located at 3494 Mistletoe Road and currently zoned R -4 
(Recreational Residential), to operate an egg sales business.  
 
The property is located on the west side of Mistletoe Road and is currently zoned R -4 (Recreational 
Residential) as are the adjacent properties. Properties on the east side of Mistletoe Road are zoned R-
A (Residential Agricultural).  
 
The applicant has applied for a business license for Five Oaks Farm with the goal of selling farm fresh 
eggs. The applicant has indicated that there are chickens and mobile chicken coops on the property 
for this purpose. Egg sales will be conducted at the farmers market as well as directly to customers on 
the farm. This type of use is considered an agricultural  use under County code; agricultural use is a 
Limited Use in the R-4 zoning district, with the limitation being that poultry houses and feedlots for the 
commercial sale of meat or eggs is prohibited.  
 
While on a strict interpretation this could negate the applicant’s entire business request, the Provisional 
Home Occupation process has previously been used for similar business es on R -1 (Single Family 
Residential) (Elduet’s Farm) and R -4 (Winkler Farm) parcels to permit appropriately scaled egg and 
meat sales businesses to operate from properties where agricultural uses are Limited. As discussed in 
those reports, the scale of the business is a key question in deciding whether this avenue is appropriate, 
or if the proposal violates the intent of the prohibition on poultry houses and feedlots.  
 
Several methods of analyzing a business proposal were covered in the previous staff report s, and 
included options for regulating these uses based on an absolute number of animals or based on the 
acreage used for the business. The previous approval utilized the percentage of the property method 
based on the areas that were fenced for the animals on that site, and considered that using less than 
20% of the property was allowable in line with the standards used for customary home occupations 
which are permitted to use up to 20% of the house area. However, for this application, this standard 
may be less applicable, as the chickens are in mobile coops that are moved daily, and therefore cover 
more area of the property, although not necessarily using all areas simultaneously.

The applicant has indicated that they have approximately 120 chickens at the present time, as well as 
6 ducks, beehives, and sheep. Currently the business request only applies to egg sales.  
 
True poultry houses are typically much larger than the applicant’s proposed business, having 
thousands or tens of thousands of chickens as compared to the 120 specified. However, the Planning 
Commission will need to determine what the appropriate number of chickens is per acre for properties 
larger than 1 acre. Properties less than 1 acre already have a cap of 6 chickens speci fied in the code. 
One possible avenue would be to extend this ratio to larger properties, which would allow around 54 
chickens on the applicant’s property, however, staff sees some flaws with this approach. For example, 
if a property as small as half an ac re could also have 6 chickens, what would prevent the maximum 
chicken density from being set higher, for example 10 or 12 chickens per acre, on larger properties? 
Chickens generally do not require large amounts of space to have adequate care, although they  can 
cover a larger area when allowed to free range as the applicant proposes. Since there is no guidance 
in the code relating to larger properties and home occupations, the Planning Commission will need to 
decide if they are comfortable with the applicant ’s requested numbers of chickens and fowl related to 
the proposed egg sales business. 
 
An additional supporting factor in this case is that properties on the opposite side of Mistletoe Road are 
zoned R-A. These properties can operate agricultural businesses, including poultry houses, egg sales, 
feedlots, etc., by right. Arguably the applicant’s property is very similar to those across the street, being 
a large acreage lot, but happens to be on the other side of the adopted zoning district divide. Depending 
on the applicant’s long- term plans for the property, it may also be worth them considering requesting 
R-A zoning for their parcel if those plans include further expansion into agricultural uses on this 
property.  
 
Given the proposed scale of the business, and the proximity to properties that are allowed similar or 
even more intense uses, this business is unlikely to negatively impact the adjacent properties and 
should be in line with the intent of the code.  
 
Staff recommends approval of the request for a Provisional Home Occupation for Tax Map 002 Parcel 
014, 9 +/- acres located at 3494 Mistletoe Road and currently zoned R-4 (Recreational Residential), to 
operate an egg sales business.

nearby property. 
It is not anticipated that the proposed use will  adversely affect the existing use or usability of 
adjacent or nearby property.

The applicant has applied for a business license for JW IT Partners, LLC. The applicant has provided 
a thorough narrative with the Provisional Home Occupation application explaining that the business is 
an e-commerce business specializing in online resale of electronics . The business receives items via 
commercial shipping (UPS/FedEx/USPS), photographs and lists the items, and then commercially 
ships them to buyers. While this type of business could be allowed as a customary home occupation, 
the applicant is requesting to use space both within the existing residence and in an existing detached 
workshop on the property. The narrative clarifies that there will be no customer traffic to the property, 
however, the applicant is additionally requesting permission to have employees on the site. The use of 
the detached building and additional employees requires review as a Provisional Home Occupation.  
 
In regards to use of the existing building, the applicant has indicated that only about 600 square feet of 
that building will be used for the business, with the remaining space being used for personal items. The 
existing residence is 3500 square feet, so the proposed 600 square feet of business space is well under 
50% of the house square footage and is approvable. The subject property is part of a large lot 
subdivision; accessory structures such as sheds and workshops are common on these properties, and 
use of a portion of the building for business -related storage rather than personal storage is unlikely to 
impact the neighboring parcels.  
 
The request to have employees on the property deserves separate consideration; the first requirement 
for a home occupation is that, “the business is conducted only by members of the family residing on 
the premises, or is conducted in such a manner that employees are not required to travel to the 
residence as part of their occupation.” The applicant’s proposal to have employees working on their 
residential property clearly violates this requirement.

the development, as well as a conceptual plan.     
 
The subject property is located on the south side of Gordon Highway. Property to the north across 
Gordon Highway is zoned M -1 (Light Industrial), property to the west , south, and east  is zoned R-A. 
There is a lone S -1 (Special) zoned parcel located north of the overall parcel along Gordon Highway 
that is zoned for a church per RZ90-12-02. This application previously came in under RZ26-10-02, but

conceptual plan shows an approximately 16,000 square foot church building located towards the front 
of the property which is proposed to have an approximately 4, 700 square foot assembly area with a 
seating capacity of 300 , a proposed 25,000 square foot educational and gym building located to the 
south of the proposed church building on the opposite side of the parking lot  that would be built in the 
future, and a paved parking lot with approximately 128 spaces located to the west and south of the 
church building. South of the parking lot Is proposed green space, an open field, baseball field (no 
lighting is proposed for the field), two playgrounds, a 3,000 square foot bathroom building, and a 4,000 
square foot storage building. The applicant proposes 30 -foot buffers where adjacent to residential 
property and a 25 -foot landscape strip along Gordon Highway. Building setbacks are proposed to be 
125 feet from the centerline of Gordon Highway and the building setbacks on the side and rear match 
the proposed 30-foot buffers. The remainder of the property would remain zoned R-A and is proposed 
to be subdivided into four lot s ranging in size from 3 acres up to 21.78 +/ - acres. Access to these lots 
is proposed via a 60-foot access easement from Gordon Highway.

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner and applicant Greenpoint Capital, LLLP  requests a variance to Section 90-98 List of lot & 
structure requirements to remove the maximum building setback in the Evans Town Center Overlay 
District on property located at 601 Ponder Place Drive, Tax map 073 Parcel 366C, 1.37 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial). The applicant has included a conceptual development 
plan and elevations, neither of which are binding.  
 
The subject property is located on the southern side of the intersection of Ponder Place Drive and North 
Belair Road. Property to the north and east is zoned P -1 (Professional) as part of the Ponder Place 
Professional Park, property to the west is zoned C -C (Community Commercial), and property to the 
south across North Belair Road is zoned P -1 and PUD (Planned Unit Development). The subject 
property was most recently rezoned earlier this year (RZ26- 05-07) to C -C and a variance (VA24- 09-
03) was approved to r emove the maximum front setback from the shared service drive only. The 
maximum setback was kept in place along both North Belair and Ponder Place with that variance.  
 
As noted, the property is in the Evans Town Center Overlay District and has a minimum building setback 
of 5 feet from the property line and a maximum building setback of 125 feet from the centerline of North 
Belair Road and 55 feet from the centerline of Ponder Place Court. This creates an “envelope” along 
the frontages where a building must touch. Previous iterations of this conceptual plan, such as the one 
shown with the rezoning from RZ26 -05-07, were able to meet this requirement, but with further 
refinement of the site plan, the applicant is now requesting to remove the maximum building setback.  
 
Per the provided narrative, to utilize the existing driveway cut, the building must  sit further back from 
North Belair Road and Ponder Place to allow for traffic flow around the building. The site does have a 
proposed drive thru on the shared drive on the western side of the property, so there is a need for traffic 
flow around the building. Additionally, with the property’s location on a corner and the disparities of the 
two setback requirements (from the property line, the max setback is 30 feet on the Ponder Place

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner and applicant Club Car, LLC (Brandon Jaremski) requests a variance to Sections 90-98 List of 
lot & structure requirements  and 90-139 Buffers & screening to reduce building setbacks and buffers 
for an existing and constructed structure on property located at 4151 Washington Road, Tax map 079 
Parcel 100, 47 +/- acres, and currently zoned M-1 (Light Industrial). The applicant has included an 
addendum and site plan with the requested variance.   
 
The subject property is located on the northern side of Washington Road. Property to the north is zoned 
R-3 (Single Family Residential) and C -2 (General Commercial), to the east is zoned R -3 and S -1 
(Special), to the south is zoned R -3, and to the east acr oss Washington Road is C -2 and S -1. The 
subject property is located within the CPOD (Corridor Protection Overlay District).  
 
In July 2026, Columbia County Building Standards was made aware of a 6,045 square foot building 
that had been constructed on the subject property without permitting. When a site plan was submitted 
for the already constructed building, it was found that the buildi ng did not meet the 30- foot building 
setback or the 40- foot structural buffer requirement from the adjacent residential property. The newly 
constructed building, according to the submitted plans, is approximately 22 feet 8 inches from the 
property line and the existing building also shown on those submitted plans is approximately 26 feet 10 
inches from the property line respectively.      
 
Per the provided addendum, the recently constructed building was built to align with the existing 
building shown on the provided site plan and to allow room for tractor trailers to be able to turn around 
in front of the building. The building is sized for the storage and work area needed to support Club Car’s 
engineering team. Due to the topography of the area, the building is approximately 8 feet below the 
adjacent residential neighborhood. At the top of the hill, adjacent to the residential neighborhood, an 
existing 6-foot chain link fence with fabric provides a visual screen from the residential neighborhood

and the building aligns with the top of that fence. The applicant also notes that there is no lighting along 
the back of the building or  mechanical equipment that could be a nuisance to the adjacent residential 
use. Lastly, the applicant also asserts that the building provides a sound barrier from the tractor trailers 
on the property and the residential neighborhood.  
 
When an industrial use is located adjacent to residential uses, particular attention must be given to 
buffering and screening between those two dissimilar uses. When Club Car was originally developed, 
a 10-foot structural buffer was all that was typically required between such uses, but over time, this 
increased substantially to 40 feet to provide a better measure of protection to those adjacent residential 
uses. However, topography can help in situations like this where the more intense use, Club Car in this 
case, is located below the adjacent residential uses. Structural buffers can be enhanced by the 
topographical difference and be more effective than if the uses did not have a significant grade 
difference. In staff’s opinion, that fact is essentially the saving grace with this application. Without it, 
there would be serious discussion about the building’s viability with its location. However, based on the 
topographical difference, staff does see a solution tha t works for the applicant, while balancing the 
needs of the adjacent property.  
 
However, there is some concern about how to effectively buffer the area due to not only the slope, but 
also the existing power lines in the area and the need for Fire Department access around the entirety 
of the building. A structural buffer is intended to include an opaque fence and plantings within the buffer 
area. In this case, the structural component is a chain link fence with fabric which is technically opaque 
and is located on the top of the slope. The issue is that the area available to plan t, due to the 
topography, is an approximately 6-foot flat section on the interior side of the fence. To further complicate 
matters, the overhead power for the site runs along this property line, which limits the ability to plant 
trees within this buffer area. Additionally, the Fire Department has noted that access around the building 
is a concern and has conveyed to staff that planting the slope is not recommended. Due to this, the 
only realistic plant material in this area will be shrubs that are planted to meet the requirement instead 
of trees. This can be worked out during Plan Review with the design engineer, Planning, and Fire 
Department staff.  
 
In regard to lighting and mechanical units, staff does propose a condition that no lighting be permitted 
on the rear of the constructed building and if the adjacent building has existing lighting a photometric 
plan showing footcandle readings of 0 at the residential property line will be required to be submitted 
with the site plan currently in for review. Lastly, staff does want to clarify that this request only reduces 
the buffers and setbacks in this limited area, not the entirety of the site. Any future buildings or 
expansions of existing buildings that meet the threshold to require a variance will be submitted prior to 
any work taking place.   
 
Due to the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends to approve with conditions the request for a 
variance to  Sections 90-98 List of lot & structure requirements  and 90- 139 Buffers & screening  to 
reduce building setbacks and buffers to 20 feet for an existing and constructed structure on property 
located at 4151 Washington Road, Tax map 079 Parcel 100, 47 +/ - acres, and currently zoned M -1 
(Light Industrial).

protection overlay district  to allow an overhead door facing Washington Road on property  located at

Commercial). The applicant has provided a brief addendum and photos of the site showing the 
improvements made in conjunction with the overhead door. This request does come from a Code 
Enforcement action.  
 
The subject property is located on the southern side of Washington Road. All adjacent and nearby 
property is zoned C-2 (General Commercial).  
 
The subject property is in  the CPOD (Corridor Protection Overlay District) which does not permit an 
overhead door to face a frontage. They are only permitted on the side or rear of a building. The applicant 
has installed a glass roll up door on the frontage of the subject property to  allow for vehicular access 
to the unit he is using to operate his business which outfits public safety vehicles. This was done without 
permitting which prompted the Code Enforcement action. Per the provided addendum, the applicant 
chose the glass door for  its aesthetic appeal and to match other businesses in the area and all glass 
front of the building. Also noted is that the applicant has installed additional landscaping along the side 
of the building and new signage to improve the aesthetics of the building.

glass or similar roll up doors when a roll up door must face a frontage or even side of a building. 
Examples include Jim Hudson Lexus and Take 5 as just two examples. While not being the result of a 
variation, the Headway Collision building located at 3682 Washington Road also has a similar door.

show how well it blends into the building. However, there is typically some mitigation requested with

ITEM: Resolution Number 26-30 Halting the Acceptance of New Data Center Zoning Applications 
  
BACKGROUND: The Board has expressed concern with the potential for additional data center 
applications within the County and desires an opportunity to debate the regulations related to the same 
uses.  The Board desires to review the existing data center regulations and adopt a hold on new data 
center zoning applications within the County in order to give the Board the opportunity to consider the 
proposed text amendment to Chapter 90, Zoning in Columbia County. 
This hold shall be in effect for 365 days from the date of adoption of this Resolution on December 01, 2026, 
or until such time the Board adopts text amendments pertaining to all of the above-referenced Code 
sections. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approving Resolution Number 26-30.

 WHEREAS, the Board is considering text amendments to Chapter 90 of the 
Columbia County Code of Ordinance (the “Code”). 
 
 WHEREAS, the Board believes that there is sufficient level of concern to warrant 
the hold. 
 
 NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board and it is hereby resolved by 
the authority of same as follows: 
 
 Section 1. Purpose.  The Board has expressed concern with the potential for 
additional data center applications within the County and desires an opportunity to debate 
the regulations related to the same uses.  The Board desires to review the existing data 
center regulations and adopt a hold on new data center zoning applications within the 
County in order to give the Board the opportunity to consider the proposed text 
amendment to Chapter 90, Zoning in Columbia County. 
 
 Section 2. Reasons for the Hold.  The Board is concerned about property owners 
possibly seeking to apply for and/or obtain data center zoning approvals during the period 
of time that it will take for the said text amendments to be considered and voted upon the 
Board.  The Board is aware that one of the best attributes of the County is its quality of 
life and its development as a suburban/rural area.  The Board feels that it is important to 
protect the quality of life in the County.  While the Board does not find the County’s 
ordinances are deficient, it does find that a hold is appropriate to give the Board time to 
consider adoption of the proposed text amendments without being subject to property 
owners possibly seeking to erect new data centers within the County and avoid certain 
changes that the proposed text amendments will make if adopted during the period of 
time that said text amendments are under consideration for adoption. 
 
 Section 3. Effective Date and Term.  Effective on the adoption of this Resolution, 
Columbia County imposes a hold and shall not accept applications for new Data Centers 
to consider proposed text amendments related to the same.  This hold shall be in effect 
for 365 days from the date of adoption of this Resolution on December 01, 2026 or until 
such time the Board adopts text amendments pertaining to all of the above referenced 
Code sections. 
 
 Section 4.  Repeal of conflicting resolutions.  Any resolutions in conflict with 
this Resolution are hereby repealed to the extent necessary to eliminate such conflict. 
 
 Section 5.  Effective Date.  This Resolution shall be effective immediately upon 
its adoption. 
 
 Adopted this 1st day of December, 2026.

ITEM: United Healthcare Employee Medical Insurance Renewal for Year 2027

insurance product for year 2027. This renewal includes an increase in the Administrative Services Fee

ITEM: Ancillary Dwelling Variance for Tax Map 040 Parcel 147 
  
BACKGROUND: The applicant requests approval to allow a proposed ancillary dwelling to exceed 1,800 
square feet in size on property located at 5771 Lanette Lane, Tax Map 040 Parcel 147, 4.32 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural). An ancillary dwelling may not be over 1,800 square feet 
under roof unless the Board of Commissioners waives that requirement based on the size of the lot, the 
size of the principal dwelling, the topography of the lot, proximity of the proposed ancillary dwelling to other 
structures, and any other factors which might affect the aesthetics of placing the ancillary dwelling on the 
lot. 
 
The applicant proposes to construct a multi-purpose ancillary residence and garage structure on an existing 
slab. The proposed layout plans for 1,016 square feet of residential space and 1,023 square feet of garage 
space for a total of 2,039 square feet. The residential space will feature a single bedroom, living room, 
kitchen, bathroom, and foyer with an entrance to a separate garage space devoted exclusively to serving 
this residential space. Since we view total square footage under roof, the total area exceeds the 1,800 
square feet permitted for an ancillary dwelling to be permitted without the variance. However, as shown, the 
area of the residential space at 1,016 square feet is under the required 1,800 square feet and the garage 
area takes up the majority of the additional space under roof. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of the request to exceed 1,800 square feet in size 
for an ancillary dwelling on property located at 5771 Lanette Lane, Tax Map 040 Parcel 147, 4.32 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owners Winston and Wanda Suggs and applicant Tully Frost request approval to allow a proposed 
ancillary dwelling to exceed 1,800 square feet in size on property located at 5 771 Lanette Lane, Tax 
Map 040 Parcel 147, 4.32 +/- acres, and currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).  
 
The subject property is located on the nor th side of Lanette  Lane. All adjacent property is zoned R -A 
(Residential Agricultural).  
 
Per Columbia County code, an ancillary dwelling may not be over 1,800 square feet under roof unless 
the Board of Commissioners waives that requirement based on the size of the lot, the size of the 
principal dwelling, the topography of the lot, proximity of  the proposed ancillary dwelling to other 
structures, and any other factors which might affect the aesthetics of placing the ancillary dwelling on 
the lot. 
 
The applicant proposes to construct a multi -purpose ancillary residence and garage structure on an 
existing slab. The proposed layout plans for 1,016 square feet of residential space and 1,023 square 
feet of garage space for a total of 2,039 square feet. The residential space will feature a single bedroom, 
living room, kitchen, bathroom, and foyer with an entrance to a separate garage space  devoted 
exclusively to serving this residential space.  Since we view total square footage under roof, the total 
area exceeds the 1,800 square feet permitted for an ancillary dwelling to be permitted without the 
variance.  
 
As noted, there is an existing slab that the applicant is seeking to build a 2,039 square foot combination 
garage and residential structure on. However, it should be noted that the actual area for the living space 
is 1,016 square feet. The lot is 4.32 acres in size, so it is well above the minimum size required (20,000 
square feet or 0.46 acres) to have an ancillary dwelling. Staff is not aware of any topographical issues 
on the property. Garages and ancillary dwellings, both separate and combined, are often found in these

Based on the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends approval  of the request to exceed 1,800

ITEM: Ancillary Dwelling Variance for Tax Map 009 Parcel 008 
  
BACKGROUND: The applicant requests approval to expand an existing ancillary dwelling to exceed 1,800 
square feet in size on property located at 7115 Bill Dorn Rd, Tax Map 009 Parcel 008, 36.142 +/- acres, 
and currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).  
 
Per Columbia County code, an ancillary dwelling may not be over 1,800 square feet under roof unless the 
Board of Commissioners waives that requirement based on the size of the lot, the size of the principal 
dwelling, the topography of the lot, proximity of the proposed ancillary dwelling to other structures, and any 
other factors which might affect the aesthetics of placing the ancillary dwelling on the lot. 
 
The applicant proposes to construct an addition to the existing ancillary dwelling. The current dwelling is 
860 square feet, the proposed layout plans for an additional 1,331 square feet of residential space, for a 
combined 2,191 square feet. Since we view total square footage under roof, the total area exceeds the 
1,800 square feet permitted for an ancillary dwelling to be permitted without the variance.  
 
As noted, there is an existing ancillary dwelling that the applicant is seeking to expand to 2,191 square feet. 
The lot is over 36 acres in size, so it is well above the minimum size required (20,000 square feet or .46 
acres) to have an ancillary dwelling. The proposed expansion maintains the existing building line preserving 
all current separation distances to property boundaries and the adjacent parcel’s structures and will not 
affect the other dwelling on this parcel. Staff is not aware of any topographical issues on the property. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of the request to exceed 1,800 square feet in 
size for an ancillary dwelling on property located at 7115 Bill Dorn Road, Tax Map 009 Parcel 008, 
36.142 +/- acres, and currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).

Upon Termination, a 3 month extension period will be added to the last active period. For example, if the contract
terminates at the end of a 12 month policy period, the stop loss coverage will convert to a 15 month accumulation period.
For Individual Stop Loss, the ISL level for the active period will apply to the ISL Terminal Liability Protection.  Claims paid
during both the active period and the 3 month run-out extension period will accumulate to the ISL level. The ISL accumulation
will not reset to zero at the beginning of the 3 month run-out extension period.
For Aggregate Stop Loss, the attachment point in the year of termination equals the sum of the active period attachment
point and the attachment point of the 3 month run-out extension period. The attachment point for the 3 month
extension period equals:
Run-out attachment point per subscriber times average exposures for the last three months before cancellation times two.
The attachment point per subscriber per month (PEPM) during the 3 month extension period equals the fully mature
attachment point for the immediately preceding active period.  In other words, the attachment point (PEPM) will increase
to the mature level if termination occurs at the end of the first policy year.  It will remain mature if the termination
occurs at the end of a renewal year.

ITEM: Ancillary Dwelling Variance for Tax Map 040 Parcel 147 
  
BACKGROUND: The applicant requests approval to allow a proposed ancillary dwelling to exceed 1,800 
square feet in size on property located at 5771 Lanette Lane, Tax Map 040 Parcel 147, 4.32 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural). An ancillary dwelling may not be over 1,800 square feet 
under roof unless the Board of Commissioners waives that requirement based on the size of the lot, the 
size of the principal dwelling, the topography of the lot, proximity of the proposed ancillary dwelling to other 
structures, and any other factors which might affect the aesthetics of placing the ancillary dwelling on the 
lot. 
 
The applicant proposes to construct a multi-purpose ancillary residence and garage structure on an existing 
slab. The proposed layout plans for 1,016 square feet of residential space and 1,023 square feet of garage 
space for a total of 2,039 square feet. The residential space will feature a single bedroom, living room, 
kitchen, bathroom, and foyer with an entrance to a separate garage space devoted exclusively to serving 
this residential space. Since we view total square footage under roof, the total area exceeds the 1,800 
square feet permitted for an ancillary dwelling to be permitted without the variance. However, as shown, the 
area of the residential space at 1,016 square feet is under the required 1,800 square feet and the garage 
area takes up the majority of the additional space under roof. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of the request to exceed 1,800 square feet in size 
for an ancillary dwelling on property located at 5771 Lanette Lane, Tax Map 040 Parcel 147, 4.32 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural). 
  
COMMITTEE COMMENTS: Forward to Consent Agenda. 
  
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION / MOTION: Approved Ancillary Dwelling Variance for tax map 040 147.

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owners Winston and Wanda Suggs and applicant Tully Frost request approval to allow a proposed 
ancillary dwelling to exceed 1,800 square feet in size on property located at 5 771 Lanette Lane, Tax 
Map 040 Parcel 147, 4.32 +/- acres, and currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).  
 
The subject property is located on the nor th side of Lanette  Lane. All adjacent property is zoned R -A 
(Residential Agricultural).  
 
Per Columbia County code, an ancillary dwelling may not be over 1,800 square feet under roof unless 
the Board of Commissioners waives that requirement based on the size of the lot, the size of the 
principal dwelling, the topography of the lot, proximity of  the proposed ancillary dwelling to other 
structures, and any other factors which might affect the aesthetics of placing the ancillary dwelling on 
the lot. 
 
The applicant proposes to construct a multi -purpose ancillary residence and garage structure on an 
existing slab. The proposed layout plans for 1,016 square feet of residential space and 1,023 square 
feet of garage space for a total of 2,039 square feet. The residential space will feature a single bedroom, 
living room, kitchen, bathroom, and foyer with an entrance to a separate garage space  devoted 
exclusively to serving this residential space.  Since we view total square footage under roof, the total 
area exceeds the 1,800 square feet permitted for an ancillary dwelling to be permitted without the 
variance.  
 
As noted, there is an existing slab that the applicant is seeking to build a 2,039 square foot combination 
garage and residential structure on. However, it should be noted that the actual area for the living space 
is 1,016 square feet. The lot is 4.32 acres in size, so it is well above the minimum size required (20,000 
square feet or 0.46 acres) to have an ancillary dwelling. Staff is not aware of any topographical issues 
on the property. Garages and ancillary dwellings, both separate and combined, are often found in these

Based on the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends approval  of the request to exceed 1,800

ITEM: Ancillary Dwelling Variance for Tax Map 009 Parcel 008 
  
BACKGROUND: The applicant requests approval to expand an existing ancillary dwelling to exceed 1,800 
square feet in size on property located at 7115 Bill Dorn Rd, Tax Map 009 Parcel 008, 36.142 +/- acres, 
and currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).  
 
Per Columbia County code, an ancillary dwelling may not be over 1,800 square feet under roof unless the 
Board of Commissioners waives that requirement based on the size of the lot, the size of the principal 
dwelling, the topography of the lot, proximity of the proposed ancillary dwelling to other structures, and any 
other factors which might affect the aesthetics of placing the ancillary dwelling on the lot. 
 
The applicant proposes to construct an addition to the existing ancillary dwelling. The current dwelling is 
860 square feet, the proposed layout plans for an additional 1,331 square feet of residential space, for a 
combined 2,191 square feet. Since we view total square footage under roof, the total area exceeds the 
1,800 square feet permitted for an ancillary dwelling to be permitted without the variance.  
 
As noted, there is an existing ancillary dwelling that the applicant is seeking to expand to 2,191 square feet. 
The lot is over 36 acres in size, so it is well above the minimum size required (20,000 square feet or .46 
acres) to have an ancillary dwelling. The proposed expansion maintains the existing building line preserving 
all current separation distances to property boundaries and the adjacent parcel’s structures and will not 
affect the other dwelling on this parcel. Staff is not aware of any topographical issues on the property. 
  
STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of the request to exceed 1,800 square feet in 
size for an ancillary dwelling on property located at 7115 Bill Dorn Road, Tax Map 009 Parcel 008, 
36.142 +/- acres, and currently zoned R-A (Residential Agricultural).

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner Billy Williams and applicant Impact Community Church request a rezoning from R-A (Residential 
Agricultural) to S-1 (Special) for a proposed church and associated uses on a portion of property located 
at 3894 Gordon Highway, Tax map 043 portion of Parcel 130, 13.88 +/- acres out of a total of 50 acres, 
and currently zoned R -A (Residential Agricultural).  The applicant has included a narrative describing 
the development, as well as a conceptual plan.     
 
The subject property is located on the south side of Gordon Highway. Property to the north across 
Gordon Highway is zoned M -1 (Light Industrial), property to the west , south, and east  is zoned R-A. 
There is a lone S -1 (Special) zoned parcel located north of the overall parcel along Gordon Highway 
that is zoned for a church per RZ90-12-02. This application previously came in under RZ26-10-02, but 
was increased in acreage and this application replaced it.  
 
Per the provided concept and narrative, the applicant proposes a church and associated uses. The 
conceptual plan shows an approximately 16,000 square foot church building located towards the front 
of the property which is proposed to have an approximately 4, 700 square foot assembly area with a 
seating capacity of 300 , a proposed 25,000 square foot educational and gym building located to the 
south of the proposed church building on the opposite side of the parking lot  that would be built in the 
future, and a paved parking lot with approximately 128 spaces located to the west and south of the 
church building. South of the parking lot Is proposed green space, an open field, baseball field (no 
lighting is proposed for the field), two playgrounds, a 3,000 square foot bathroom building, and a 4,000 
square foot storage building. The applicant proposes 30 -foot buffers where adjacent to residential 
property and a 25 -foot landscape strip along Gordon Highway. Building setbacks are proposed to be 
125 feet from the centerline of Gordon Highway and the building setbacks on the side and rear match 
the proposed 30-foot buffers. The remainder of the property would remain zoned R-A and is proposed 
to be subdivided into four lot s ranging in size from 3 acres up to 21.78 +/ - acres. Access to these lots 
is proposed via a 60-foot access easement from Gordon Highway.

Regarding operation of the church, services will be held on Sunday mornings between 6AM and 1PM. 
Normal office hours will be Monday through Friday from 8AM to 5PM. The church is proposed to be 
open in the evenings for groups, but the narrative notes that the schedule of group meetings would 
change depending on the semester. There are currently no programs established for the outdoor fields. 
Activities will take place on the fields during normal church hours and other appointed times. Since 
there will be no outdoor lighting, activities on the fields and playgrounds will be limited to daylight hours. 
The applicant has noted that the church does not have plans to operate a school currently.  
 
Overall, staff is in support of the request . Churches can generally operate throughout the County, 
considering any traffic concerns or any activities, typically outdoor, that may impact adjacent property. 
The applicant has proposed two fields on the back of the property but  has proposed a 30 foot natural 
buffer and no lighting for these fields, so there should be no impact on adjacent R -A properties in this 
case. No traffic concerns have been raised by either GDOT or Columbia County regarding this 
application specifically, but any required turn lanes or similar will come from GDOT since it is a GDOT 
road. In addition, due to its proximity to both Fort Gordon and the City of Harlem, they were both asked 
for any comments or conditions on this request, and none were provided.  
 
Regarding conditions, the Health Department has requested two in regard to septic systems on the 
site. While not a condition, the Fire Department and Fire Marshal have been in contact with the 
applicant’s engineer regarding fire protection which will be handled during plan review for the site and

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner and applicant Greenpoint Capital, LLLP  requests a variance to Section 90-98 List of lot & 
structure requirements to remove the maximum building setback in the Evans Town Center Overlay 
District on property located at 601 Ponder Place Drive, Tax map 073 Parcel 366C, 1.37 +/- acres, and 
currently zoned C-C (Community Commercial). The applicant has included a conceptual development 
plan and elevations, neither of which are binding.  
 
The subject property is located on the southern side of the intersection of Ponder Place Drive and North 
Belair Road. Property to the north and east is zoned P -1 (Professional) as part of the Ponder Place 
Professional Park, property to the west is zoned C -C (Community Commercial), and property to the 
south across North Belair Road is zoned P -1 and PUD (Planned Unit Development). The subject 
property was most recently rezoned earlier this year (RZ26- 05-07) to C -C and a variance (VA24- 09-
03) was approved to r emove the maximum front setback from the shared service drive only. The 
maximum setback was kept in place along both North Belair and Ponder Place with that variance.  
 
As noted, the property is in the Evans Town Center Overlay District and has a minimum building setback 
of 5 feet from the property line and a maximum building setback of 125 feet from the centerline of North 
Belair Road and 55 feet from the centerline of Ponder Place Court. This creates an “envelope” along 
the frontages where a building must touch. Previous iterations of this conceptual plan, such as the one 
shown with the rezoning from RZ26 -05-07, were able to meet this requirement, but with further 
refinement of the site plan, the applicant is now requesting to remove the maximum building setback.  
 
Per the provided narrative, to utilize the existing driveway cut, the building must  sit further back from 
North Belair Road and Ponder Place to allow for traffic flow around the building. The site does have a 
proposed drive thru on the shared drive on the western side of the property, so there is a need for traffic 
flow around the building. Additionally, with the property’s location on a corner and the disparities of the 
two setback requirements (from the property line, the max setback is 30 feet on the Ponder Place

Summary and Recommendation 
 
Owner and applicant Club Car, LLC (Brandon Jaremski) requests a variance to Sections 90-98 List of 
lot & structure requirements  and 90-139 Buffers & screening to reduce building setbacks and buffers 
for an existing and constructed structure on property located at 4151 Washington Road, Tax map 079 
Parcel 100, 47 +/- acres, and currently zoned M-1 (Light Industrial). The applicant has included an 
addendum and site plan with the requested variance.   
 
The subject property is located on the northern side of Washington Road. Property to the north is zoned 
R-3 (Single Family Residential) and C -2 (General Commercial), to the east is zoned R -3 and S -1 
(Special), to the south is zoned R -3, and to the east acr oss Washington Road is C -2 and S -1. The 
subject property is located within the CPOD (Corridor Protection Overlay District).  
 
In July 2026, Columbia County Building Standards was made aware of a 6,045 square foot building 
that had been constructed on the subject property without permitting. When a site plan was submitted 
for the already constructed building, it was found that the buildi ng did not meet the 30- foot building 
setback or the 40- foot structural buffer requirement from the adjacent residential property. The newly 
constructed building, according to the submitted plans, is approximately 22 feet 8 inches from the 
property line and the existing building also shown on those submitted plans is approximately 26 feet 10 
inches from the property line respectively.      
 
Per the provided addendum, the recently constructed building was built to align with the existing 
building shown on the provided site plan and to allow room for tractor trailers to be able to turn around 
in front of the building. The building is sized for the storage and work area needed to support Club Car’s 
engineering team. Due to the topography of the area, the building is approximately 8 feet below the 
adjacent residential neighborhood. At the top of the hill, adjacent to the residential neighborhood, an 
existing 6-foot chain link fence with fabric provides a visual screen from the residential neighborhood

and the building aligns with the top of that fence. The applicant also notes that there is no lighting along 
the back of the building or  mechanical equipment that could be a nuisance to the adjacent residential 
use. Lastly, the applicant also asserts that the building provides a sound barrier from the tractor trailers 
on the property and the residential neighborhood.  
 
When an industrial use is located adjacent to residential uses, particular attention must be given to 
buffering and screening between those two dissimilar uses. When Club Car was originally developed, 
a 10-foot structural buffer was all that was typically required between such uses, but over time, this 
increased substantially to 40 feet to provide a better measure of protection to those adjacent residential 
uses. However, topography can help in situations like this where the more intense use, Club Car in this 
case, is located below the adjacent residential uses. Structural buffers can be enhanced by the 
topographical difference and be more effective than if the uses did not have a significant grade 
difference. In staff’s opinion, that fact is essentially the saving grace with this application. Without it, 
there would be serious discussion about the building’s viability with its location. However, based on the 
topographical difference, staff does see a solution tha t works for the applicant, while balancing the 
needs of the adjacent property.  
 
However, there is some concern about how to effectively buffer the area due to not only the slope, but 
also the existing power lines in the area and the need for Fire Department access around the entirety 
of the building. A structural buffer is intended to include an opaque fence and plantings within the buffer 
area. In this case, the structural component is a chain link fence with fabric which is technically opaque 
and is located on the top of the slope. The issue is that the area available to plan t, due to the 
topography, is an approximately 6-foot flat section on the interior side of the fence. To further complicate 
matters, the overhead power for the site runs along this property line, which limits the ability to plant 
trees within this buffer area. Additionally, the Fire Department has noted that access around the building 
is a concern and has conveyed to staff that planting the slope is not recommended. Due to this, the 
only realistic plant material in this area will be shrubs that are planted to meet the requirement instead 
of trees. This can be worked out during Plan Review with the design engineer, Planning, and Fire 
Department staff.  
 
In regard to lighting and mechanical units, staff does propose a condition that no lighting be permitted 
on the rear of the constructed building and if the adjacent building has existing lighting a photometric 
plan showing footcandle readings of 0 at the residential property line will be required to be submitted 
with the site plan currently in for review. Lastly, staff does want to clarify that this request only reduces 
the buffers and setbacks in this limited area, not the entirety of the site. Any future buildings or 
expansions of existing buildings that meet the threshold to require a variance will be submitted prior to 
any work taking place.   
 
Due to the reasoning outlined above, staff recommends to approve with conditions the request for a 
variance to  Sections 90-98 List of lot & structure requirements  and 90- 139 Buffers & screening  to 
reduce building setbacks and buffers to 20 feet for an existing and constructed structure on property 
located at 4151 Washington Road, Tax map 079 Parcel 100, 47 +/ - acres, and currently zoned M -1 
(Light Industrial).

Criteria for Evaluation of Variance Proposal 
 
1. There are special circumstances or conditions unique to the property that do not 
generally apply to the district.  
The only special circumstance in this case is that the area is lower than the adjacent residential 
uses and can potentially provide a more effective buffer due to this grade difference. However, 
the construction of a building without any permitting should not be repeated again on this 
property.  
 
2. The special circumstances or conditions are such that the strict application of the 
provisions of this chapter would deprive the applicant of any reasonable use of his land. 
Mere loss of value shall not justify a variance. There must be a deprivation of beneficial 
use of land.  
In order to meet setbacks and buffers, the applicant would be required to either heavily modify 
or tear down the constructed building. While it does appear that the applicant utilizes a large 
portion of this site, there is room to meet those setbacks. However, it should be noted that other 
existing buildings already do not meet the setback and buffer requirements as currently written. 
This does not absolve what happened here, but should be noted.  
 
3. Topographical or other conditions peculiar and particular to the site are such that strict 
adherence to the requirements of this chapter would cause the owner unnecessary 
hardship and would not carry out the intent of this chapter, and that there is no feasible 
alternative to remedy the situation.  
As noted, there is a grade change between the adjacent residential properties and the subject 
property. This does give the ability to potentially have a more effective buffer due to this site 
being lower than the adjacent properties. With proposed conditions, staff thinks this can be 
accomplished.

Motion by Commissioner Riden, seconded by Commissioner Park to approve the agenda as 
presented. Motion passed unanimously. 
  
EXTENSION OF THE DATA CENTER MORATORIUM 
The Board discussed extending the current temporary moratorium on data centers. Planning staff 
reported receiving several inquiries regarding data centers and stated that proposed regulations 
were being developed. Staff had conducted research and visited several sites in Georgia to better 
understand the impacts of data centers on surrounding communities. Staff requested a 120-day 
extension to complete the zoning process and present proposed regulations to the Planning 
Commission and Board of Commissioners for review. 
Motion by Commissioner Riden, seconded by Commissioner Park, to approve Resolution 2026-RES-009, 
Moratorium on Applications for Data Centers, extending the existing temporary moratorium by 120 days, 
and place the item on the consent agenda for the next meeting. Motion passed unanimously. 
 
EXTENSION OF THE PLANNED UNIT DEVELOPMENT MORATORIUM 
 
The Board discussed extending the current temporary moratorium on Planned Unit 
Developments. Planning staff reported that work on the proposed regulations had been underway 
for several months. However, competing priorities involving data centers and solar farms had 
delayed completion of the final draft for public distribution and feedback from one of the 
County’s two Planned Unit Developments. 
Staff requested a 120-day extension to complete the draft and obtain public comments before 
submitting the proposed regulations to the Planning Commission and Board of Commissioners 
for review. 
Motion by Commissioner Park, seconded by Commissioner Jones, to approve Resolution 2026-
RES-010, extending the existing temporary moratorium on Planned Unit Developments for 120 
days, and to place the item on the consent agenda for the next meeting. Motion passed 
unanimously. 
DEMOLITION OF FORMER MORGAN COUNTY JAIL 
 
Staff reported that demolition of the former Morgan County Jail is necessary before 
improvements to the Ag Center and construction of the 4-H indoor shooting sports facility can 
proceed. Both projects were specifically identified in the SPLOST referendum. 
A request for proposals was issued on July 20, 2026, and bids were received on September 24, 
2026. Following review, the County’s engineer recommended awarding the demolition contract

Repair Project to East Coast Grading in the amount of $863,704.50 and to place the item on the 
consent agenda for the next meeting. Motion passed unanimously. 
GODFREY ROAD DRAINAGE REPAIR 
Staff reported that the culvert on Godfrey Road at the county line needs replacement. An 
Invitation to Bid was issued, resulting in five qualifying bids. Dirt Works Grading and 
Construction submitted the lowest bid of $76,553.00. 
Staff requested an additional 15% contingency to cover unsuitable soil or other unexpected 
expenses that may arise once the existing structure is removed, bringing the total proposed 
amount to $88,035.95. 
Motion by Commissioner von Hanstein, seconded by Commissioner Jones, to award the Godfrey 
Road culvert replacement project to Dirt Works Grading and Construction in an amount not to 
exceed $88,035.95, including a 15% contingency, to be funded by TSPLOST, and to place the 
item on the consent agenda for the next meeting. Motion passed unanimously. 
LIVESTREAM MEETINGS FOR ELECTIONS BOARD, ASSESSORS BOARD, AND 
PLANNING & ZONING BOARD 
The Board discussed expanding livestreaming to meetings of the Board of Elections, Board of 
Assessors, and Planning and Zoning Board held in the formal meeting chamber, where 
livestreaming equipment is installed. 
Staff reported that the Board approved livestreaming and archiving its meetings in July 2025, 
with recordings retained for 90 days following approval of the minutes. The process had operated 
successfully for the past 15 months, allowing residents to view meetings live or access archived 
recordings. At the time of the initial approval, the Board expressed interest in extending 
livestreaming to other boards once the system’s reliability had been confirmed and any technical 
issues resolved. 
Motion by Commissioner Park, seconded by Commissioner Jones, to move the item to 
Unfinished Business at the November 3, 2026, Board of Commissioners meeting. Motion passed 
unanimously.
